summary: Write, from the code, how a tester reaches each Chrome item, using the cheap model
logs: paths: 773 items returned for 773 asked; 0 areas returned nothing

items.where: Side panel > composer area shows "Sign in to start chatting in Chrome." > Sign in
steps: Open the AGI side panel in Chrome while signed out (click the AGI toolbar icon).
Read the notice in the composer area: "Sign in to start chatting in Chrome."
Click the "Sign in" button. A new tab opens on the AGI sign-in page.
Finish signing in in that tab, return to the side panel and click "Check sign-in".
Compare: the side panel should show you as signed in and the chat should be usable, as Expected says.
items.needs: an AGI account (email or outside provider login)

labels.text: Sign in to start chatting in Chrome.

items.note: The same sign-in also opens from Options > Account > Sign in and from the welcome page's Sign in button. The sign-in tab goes to /sign-in, which apps/web/next.config.ts redirects to /login.

items.where: Side panel > Sign in > create a new account on the AGI sign-in page that opens in a new tab
steps: Open the AGI side panel while signed out.
Click "Sign in" in the composer area.
In the new tab that opens, look for the option to create a new account (wording not verified in the extension code).
Create an account with email or a provider, then return to the side panel and click "Check sign-in".
Compare: the new account should reach a signed-in state in the side panel, as Expected says.
items.needs: a new email address or an outside account (Google)
items.note: The extension has no sign-up screen of its own. It only hands off to the web sign-in page (/sign-in, redirected to /login in apps/web/next.config.ts), and apps/web/features/auth/authRoutes.ts defines /signup. The exact create-account wording is on the web page and was not confirmed in the code.

items.needs: a Free account, with the Terms version changed on the server
items.note: The extension has no Terms acceptance screen. apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/freeTrialClient.ts only turns a TERMS_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED error into a block message to accept the updated Terms on agiworkforce.com. Acceptance is recorded on the web at apps/web/app/signup/complete/RecordTermsAcceptance.tsx. I searched apps/extension/src for terms, Terms of Service and terms_required and found no acceptance control.

items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: No memory setup step or memory-use choice was found in apps/extension/src. The closest screens are the side panel account menu > Memory (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts, label "Memory", sheet intro "What AGI remembers about you in every app...") and Options > Account > Your account > Memory > Open, which opens the web memory settings. I searched apps/extension/src for memory, spMemory and remember strings.

items.where: Options > Account > Desktop app > Pair with Desktop
steps: Open the Options page: click "Open settings" on the welcome page, or open the AGI extension's Options from Chrome's extensions menu.
Click "Account" in the left navigation and scroll to "Desktop app".
Click "Pair with Desktop", type the code shown by AGI Desktop in the field (placeholder ABCD-EFGH), then click "Confirm Code".
Compare: the status should change from "Not paired" to paired, and the "Unpair" button should appear, as Expected says.
Click "Unpair", read the message "Unpair the desktop app? ...", then click "Unpair" again or "Keep paired" to check the way back out.
items.needs: AGI Desktop app open and showing a pairing code
items.note: Options nav labels are Permissions, Shortcuts, Options, Account and Help. The pairing rows are built in apps/extension/src/features/options/desktop-pairing-rows.ts and placed in the Account section by apps/extension/src/features/options/destinations.ts. The side panel's Desktop connection menu label is not shown in the side panel UI found in code.

items.where: Options > Options > Task completion notifications
steps: Open the Options page: click "Open settings" on the welcome page, or open the AGI extension's Options from Chrome's extensions menu.
Click "Options" in the left navigation.
Find the "Task completion notifications" row and read its hint.
Switch the toggle off and back on. Compare: the status reads "Task completion notifications are off." or "...are on."
Compare the toggle with Expected: it is optional and can be changed later.
items.needs: none
items.note: No first-run notification primer was found. The toggle is on by default (apps/extension/src/features/options/notifications-row.ts reads agi_task_notifications with a default of true), so declining means switching it off on the Options page.

items.where: Side panel, first open after install > "Getting started with AGI" bar above the composer > Next > Let's go
steps: Install AGI, or use a profile where the side panel tour has not been finished, then open the AGI side panel.
Read the first tour step above the composer: "AGI reads a page only when you attach it or ask it to act there."
Click "Next" and read the shortcuts step.
Click "Let's go" to finish the tour.
Compare: the bar should go away and the composer should be ready for a first chat, as Expected says.
items.needs: a fresh install or a profile whose tour is not finished
items.note: The tour is mounted by apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/onboardingPrompt.ts above the composer (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts). It finishes on the shortcuts step and does not itself start a chat. After install, the welcome page (apps/extension/src/features/onboarding/welcome-page.ts) opens first, with an "Open side panel" button.

items.where: Side panel header > New chat (pen icon)
steps: Open the AGI side panel while signed in.
Click the pen icon in the header whose tooltip and accessible name is New chat.
Look for an empty chat with the composer ready to type in.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: If an unsent draft is open, the panel shows "Send or clear your draft before leaving this unsent chat." instead of starting a new chat. The command palette (Ctrl/Cmd+K) also has New chat.

items.where: Side panel header > Recent chats (clock icon)
steps: Click the clock icon in the header to open Recent chats.
Click a chat title in the list.
Look for that chat's transcript and check that the composer lets you send a new message to continue it.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one saved chat
items.note: The command palette (Ctrl/Cmd+K) > Search chats opens the same Recent chats list.

items.where: Side panel header > Recent chats (clock icon) > Search recent chats
steps: Click the clock icon in the header to open Recent chats.
Click the Search recent chats field and type a word from a past chat title or message.
Check that only matching past chats are listed.
Click one of them and check that its transcript opens.
items.needs: a signed-in account with several saved chats
items.note: The search field is in the Recent chats sheet, not a separate page. Code for matching titles and message text was not checked in detail.

items.needs: a signed-in account with projects
items.note: No Projects index screen found in apps/extension. Project choices appear only in the chat history menu (Move to project, Add to project) and as a Projects group when typing @ in the composer. Searched the locale file and src for Projects, project list and project keys.

items.needs: a signed-in account with a project
items.note: No project overview screen found in apps/extension. The only project element is the chip that reads "Project · NAME" with a clear button, shown after a project is selected. Searched the locale file and src for project keys.

items.needs: a signed-in account with a project that has chats
items.note: No list of project conversations found in apps/extension. Searched the locale file and src for project keys.

items.needs: a signed-in account with a project
items.note: No project instructions editor found in apps/extension. Searched the locale file for instruction and project keys and src for project screens.

items.where: AI Assistant button above the composer > AGI Work switch; recent work under More (...) > Tasks
steps: Click the AI Assistant button above the composer to open the model menu.
Turn on the AGI Work switch.
Type a goal in the composer and send it. Check that a multi-step AGI Work run starts.
Click More (...) > Tasks and check that the run appears in the list of recent work.
items.needs: a paid account with the AGI Work capability (a Free account sees a gated note instead)
items.note: The button shows AI Assistant by default and the current model name after a model is chosen. The AGI Work switch appears only when the plan allows it.

items.where: More (...) > Tasks
steps: Click More (...) in the header, then click Tasks.
Look at the list: each row shows a title, a state label and a time.
Check whether any finished tasks can be hidden or filtered out.
Click All tasks on the web at the bottom to compare the full list.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one running or finished task
items.note: The Tasks sheet has no filter control in the code, so the Expected filter between active and finished tasks was not found. Only Stop appears on live tasks.

items.where: More (...) > Tasks > Open on a task row
steps: Click More (...) in the header, then click Tasks.
Click Open on a task row.
Look for a new browser tab on the AGI web app at that task's chat.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a task that has a conversation
items.note: The side panel shows only the title, state and time. Status, steps, outputs and pending decisions are expected on the web page, which the extension code does not show.

items.needs: a signed-in account with pending approvals
items.note: No approvals inbox found in apps/extension. Approvals appear inside a chat (Approve / Decline) and in the Schedules list for paused steps (Approve / Deny). Searched the locale file and src for approval and inbox keys.

items.where: More (...) > Shortcuts > Schedules
steps: Click More (...) in the header, then click Shortcuts. This opens the settings page on Shortcuts.
Scroll to the Schedules heading.
Click New schedule, fill in Name, Instructions and Repeat, then click Create schedule.
In the list, use Pause or Resume, Run now, Edit and Delete on a row, and check each result against Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The schedule manager sits inside the Shortcuts page of the options settings, not in its own destination. Schedule... in a chat's history menu opens the same page with a draft.

items.where: More (...) > Shortcuts > Schedules > a schedule row > Runs
steps: Open the Schedules section as in S4.17.
Click Runs on a schedule row.
Look for the Instructions text (shown under Prompt), the Next and Last times on the row, and the list of past runs under Runs.
items.needs: a schedule that has at least one run
items.note: Cadence is not shown on the row or in the runs block. The Repeat setting is visible only in the create form, and it is hidden while editing.

items.needs: a signed-in account with generated artifacts
items.note: No artifact gallery found in apps/extension. Artifacts appear as cards inside a chat reply (Artifacts in this reply, with Open and Hide). Searched the locale file and src for gallery and artifact list keys.

items.where: More (...) > Usage, or Options > Account > Plan and usage > Open
steps: Click More (...) in the header and read the Usage row, which shows a percent meter.
Click Usage. A new tab opens the AGI web usage page.
Compare the usage windows, reset times and history on that page with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account (the Usage row is hidden on the Free plan)
items.note: The extension shows only a percent meter. The per-window and reset detail is on the web page, which the extension code does not render. The web page content was not checked.

items.where: More (...) > Extension settings > Options (left menu); Account for the autofill profile
steps: Click More (...) in the header, then click Extension settings. This opens the Permissions page.
Click Options in the left menu. Change a notification setting or the Theme under Appearance.
Click Account in the left menu and open Autofill profile (optional). Change a field and save it.
Reopen the page and check that the changes were kept.
items.needs: none
items.note: More (...) > Settings opens the web settings page instead. The autofill profile is saved on this device, not in the account. The save button label for the profile was not checked.

items.where: More (...) > Help
steps: Click More (...) in the header, then click Help. This opens the settings page on Help.
Check the Help center, Documentation and Contact support rows. Each has an Open link that opens the AGI web app in a new tab.
Look for a way to send product feedback or a bug report inside the product.
items.needs: none
items.note: No in-product feedback or bug report form was found in apps/extension, so that part of Expected is not met in the code. Searched the locale file and src for feedback and bug report text.

items.where: Side panel header: New chat, Recent chats and More buttons at the top; after the first message, the chat title shows in a row below the header
steps: Open the AGI side panel and sign in to a Managed Cloud account.
Send one message in the chat box.
Look at the top: the header shows the model button, Recent chats, New chat and More.
Look just below the header for the chat title row. Compare with Expected: the header shows where you are and the main actions.
items.needs: a signed-in account; the title row needs at least one message
items.note: The title row is hidden when signed out and for temporary chats.

items.where: Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on Mac) > type Computer Use > pick Computer Use under Go to
steps: Click inside the side panel.
Press Cmd+K on Mac (Ctrl+K on Windows).
Type Computer Use and pick it under Go to.
Look for the two tabs Chat and Computer Use at the top, with Computer Use active.
items.needs: none
items.note: The Chat / Computer Use tab bar is hidden in the chat view. No Projects, Code or Work mode was found in the code.

items.where: Recent chats (clock icon in the header) > Search recent chats box
steps: Click the clock icon in the header (Recent chats).
Click the box labelled Search recent chats.
Type part of a chat title.
Look that only matching chats stay in the list.
items.needs: a signed-in account or saved chats on this device
items.note: The search covers chats only. The Cmd+K palette also searches chats.

items.where: Header > New chat button (icon at the top right of the side panel)
steps: Open a chat that already has messages.
Click the New chat button in the header.
Look for an empty chat with no messages and no title row.
items.needs: none

items.where: Recent chats (clock icon in the header) > list of chat rows
steps: Click the clock icon (Recent chats).
Look for the list of recent chats with dates.
Click one chat row.
Look that the chat opens in the chat view. Compare with Expected: recent items open on selection.
items.needs: some saved chats
items.note: The list holds chats only. No recent projects or tasks section was found here.

items.where: Recent chats (clock icon in the header) > a chat row
steps: Click the clock icon (Recent chats).
Look at a row: the title and the date.
Look for the open chat: its row has a stronger background and is marked as the current page.
Click another row's title and look that its chat opens.
items.needs: two or more saved chats
a signed-in account with a project
items.note: No project rows were found in the side panel navigation. Projects appear only in the @ mention menu under Projects and as a Project name chip. I searched apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts for project rows and Projects navigation.

items.where: More (⋮) > Tasks
steps: Sign in to an AGI account.
Click the More button (⋮) at the top right.
Click Tasks.
Look for task rows with a title, a state and a time, and an Open button. Compare with Expected: tasks are shown apart from chats.

items.note: Open takes you to the chat in the web app, not inside the side panel.

items.where: More (⋮) > Tasks > the state text under a task
steps: Start a background task that is still running.
Click More (⋮) > Tasks.
Look for the state text Running under that task.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a running task
items.note: Recent chat rows have no running mark; the only one found is the state text in Tasks.

items.where: More (⋮) > Tasks > the state text under a task
steps: Start a task that asks for your input or approval.
Click More (⋮) > Tasks.
Look for Waiting for input or Waiting for approval under that task.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a task that needs input or approval
items.note: Recent chat rows have no waiting mark; the only one found is the state text in Tasks.

items.where: Recent chats (clock icon) > More actions (⋯) on a chat row
steps: Click the clock icon (Recent chats).
Click the ⋯ button at the right of a chat row.
Look for Pin, Rename, Move to project, Share, Archive and Delete chat.
Click Rename and look for the edit box.
items.needs: a saved chat
items.note: Which items appear depends on whether the chat is saved to the account. Archive and Delete ask to confirm first.

items.where: Cmd+K on Mac (Ctrl+K on Windows) with the side panel focused
steps: Click inside the side panel.
Press Cmd+K (Ctrl+K on Windows).
Look for the Commands box with the placeholder Search commands and chats.
Type New or a chat name and look for matching Go to items and Chats.
items.needs: none; the Chats list needs a signed-in account

items.where: More (⋮) > Extension settings > Options page: Options > Keyboard shortcuts
steps: Click the More button (⋮).
Click Extension settings. The Options page opens in a new tab.
Click Options in the left list.
Scroll to Keyboard shortcuts. Look for Open side panel and Send page screenshot to Desktop, each with a shortcut and a Configure button.
items.needs: none
items.note: The list shows only Chrome commands. The Cmd+K palette shortcut is not listed. The More > Shortcuts item opens saved prompts, not this list.

items.where: More (⋮) > account block at the top of the menu
steps: Sign in to an AGI account.
Click the More button (⋮) at the top right.
Look at the top of the menu: your name or email and plan name.
Look for Settings, Usage, Tasks, Memory, Upgrade plan and Log out.
items.needs: a signed-in account; Usage is not shown on the Free plan
items.note: The account block is hidden when signed out.

items.where: More (⋮) > Help
steps: Click the More button (⋮).
Click Help. The Options page opens on its Help section.
Look for Help center, Documentation and Contact support.
items.needs: none
items.note: No feedback entry was found in the Help menu or Help section.

items.where: More (⋮) > Upgrade plan
steps: Sign in to an account on a plan with a higher tier.
Click the More button (⋮).
Look for Upgrade plan and click it.
Look that a web plans page opens in a new tab.

items.note: Upgrade plan shows only when a higher tier exists. The plan file says the quota upgrade button leads to web billing behind a waitlist gate; I did not check that path.

items.where: Above the chat box: notice Desktop tools are optional and currently disconnected. > Reconnect
steps: Make sure the AGI desktop app is not running.
Open the side panel.
Look above the chat box for the notice text and the Reconnect button.
Click Reconnect and look for a change in the notice.
items.needs: the AGI desktop app not running

labels.text: Desktop tools are optional and currently disconnected.

items.note: The notice covers desktop tools only. No general cloud connection indicator was found.

items.where: Header > Recent chats (clock icon); the list opens as a full overlay over the panel
steps: Drag the Chrome side panel to its narrowest width.
Click the clock icon (Recent chats).
Look for the list filling the panel with a Close button.
Click Close and look that focus returns to the clock icon.
items.needs: a narrow side panel; Chrome side panels cannot reach phone width
items.note: No slide-in drawer was found in the code. Recent chats is a full overlay opened from a header button, with focus returned on close.

items.where: Page and panel backgrounds across the whole side panel; they change when the theme changes under Extension settings > Options > Theme
steps: Click the More button (⋮) at the top right of the side panel, then click Extension settings to open the Options page.
Click Options in the left list, find the Appearance section and the Theme select.
Choose Light, then Dark, then System, and go back to the side panel after each choice.
Compare the page background and panel backgrounds in each theme: each should change as a whole with no leftover fixed colours.
items.needs: none

items.where: Click the More (⋮) button in the side panel header; the menu is the raised surface
steps: Click the More (⋮) button at the top right of the side panel.
Look at the menu panel against the chat background behind it.
Switch the theme to Light and then Dark under Extension settings > Options > Theme and open More again.
Compare: the menu should look raised above the page in both themes, as a separate surface.
items.needs: none
items.note: The code sets the menu surface through the shared tokens; the exact elevation was not measured.

items.where: Reply text and muted caption text in the chat, such as the small row under a message
steps: Send any message in the chat and wait for a reply.
Read the reply text and the small muted row under the message.
Switch the theme to Light and then Dark under Extension settings > Options > Theme and look again.
Compare: primary and muted text should both stay readable on the panel background in both themes.
items.needs: a chat reply (signed-in account not verified in code)
items.note: A 4.5:1 contrast ratio needs a colour meter; the tester can only check readability by eye.

items.where: The border around the message box at the bottom of the chat and the border of the More menu
steps: Click the More (⋮) button and look at the edge of the menu.
Look at the edge of the message box at the bottom of the side panel.
Switch the theme to Dark under Extension settings > Options > Theme and look at both edges again.
Compare: both borders should be visible but subtle, in both themes.
items.needs: none

items.where: Accent colour on the model selector button in the chat header, and the text selection highlight in a reply
steps: Drag across a line of reply text to select it and look at the selection highlight.
Look at the accent-tinted model selector button in the chat header.
Switch the theme to Light and then Dark under Extension settings > Options > Theme and repeat.
Compare: the selection and accent colours should stay readable with the text on them in both themes.
items.needs: a chat reply
items.note: The on-fill and text roles were read in the code, not measured.

items.where: Warning or error text in the panel, for example the copy failure message
steps: Find a place where the panel shows a failure notice, such as a failed copy of a message.
Read the notice text and check that it is readable on its background.
Switch the theme to Dark under Extension settings > Options > Theme and look at the notice again.
Compare: error and status text should stay readable in both themes.
items.needs: a way to make a copy or save fail (not found in code)
items.note: Triggering a real failure was not confirmed, and status colours for success, warning and info were not checked on screen.

items.where: Font faces in chat text, headings and code blocks
steps: Send a message and read the reply text in the chat.
Find a code block in a reply, or ask for one.
Compare the sans-serif text with the monospace code text.
Compare: the UI font, the editorial font and the monospace font should each look like one declared family.
items.needs: a chat reply with code
items.note: The editorial family was not confirmed on screen; the code declares UI and monospace families in side_panel.ts.

items.where: Headings in a chat reply
steps: Ask the chat for an answer with a heading, a sub-heading and a small heading.
Look at the three heading levels in the reply.
Compare: each level should have a clear step in size and weight, the same across replies.
items.needs: a chat reply with headings
items.note: Whether a reply returns headings depends on the model, and the sizes were read from tokens, not measured.

items.where: Body text in the chat and in the menus
steps: Send a message and read the reply body text.
Compare the body text with the smaller caption text under a message.
Compare: body text should use one base size across replies.
items.needs: a chat reply
items.note: No in-app text-size control was found in apps/extension/src; respect for the OS text-size setting was not confirmed.

items.where: Caption and metadata text, such as the small row under a chat message
steps: Send a message and find the small row under the reply.
Read the caption text and compare its size with the body text.
Compare: captions should stay readable and not smaller than the small text size set in the tokens.
items.needs: a chat reply
items.note: The caption token resolves to 14px in side_panel.css, which is the small body size, not a 12px role.

items.where: Code blocks and inline code in a chat reply
steps: Ask the chat for a short code sample and wait for the reply.
Compare the code text with the body text next to it.
Compare: code should use a monospace font and a size of its own.
items.needs: a chat reply with code

items.where: Line spacing in multi-line replies, headings, body and code
steps: Send a message that gets a multi-line reply with a heading and a code block.
Compare the line spacing of body text, heading and code.
Compare: each text role should have its own line spacing that suits its size.
items.needs: a chat reply

items.where: Gap between paragraphs in a reply
steps: Ask the chat for an answer with at least three paragraphs.
Look at the gap between the paragraphs.
Compare: the gap should be the same between every pair of paragraphs.
items.needs: a chat reply with several paragraphs

items.where: Indent of bulleted and numbered lists in a reply, and nested lists
steps: Ask the chat for a list with a nested sub-list.
Look at the indent of the top list and the nested list.
Compare: each nested level should step in by the same amount.
items.needs: a chat reply with a list
items.note: The list indent rule was read only by its line number in side_panel.ts.

items.where: Padding inside code blocks in a reply
steps: Ask the chat for a code block.
Look at the space between the code text and the edge of the code box on all sides.
Compare: the padding should look the same on every side.
items.needs: a chat reply with code

items.where: Cells of a table in a reply
steps: Ask the chat for a small table with a header row.
Look at the padding in each table cell.
Compare: all cells should have the same padding and the table should not overflow the panel.
items.needs: a chat reply with a table

items.where: Space between one chat turn and the next
steps: Send two messages in a row and wait for both replies.
Look at the space between each message and the next one.
Compare: the space between turns should be the same each time.
items.needs: a chat reply

items.where: Chat: the action row directly under a message, with Copy message under your message and Copy response under a reply
steps: Send a message and wait for a reply.
Look at the row directly under your message and under the reply.
Compare the distance from each message bubble to its action row.

Click in the box and type a few words.
Compare the space between the typed text and the box edge, and around the send control.

Look at the margin between the content and the panel edge at each width.

Look at the rows in the list.
Compare: every row should have the same height, including rows with long titles.

steps: Click the More (⋮) button in the side panel header.
Look at the height of each menu item.

Compare the inner padding with the menu or other sheets you open.

items.note: The only dialog with its own padding found in the lines read is the media viewer (16px), so a single shared dialog padding was not confirmed.

Look at the Theme label, the select beneath it and the spacing between this row and the next form row.

Look at the strip just above the message box
Read the text and check the Sign in button beside it
Compare with Expected: a full-width strip with a system message and an action
items.needs: a signed-out account

labels.text: Sign in to start chatting in Chrome.

items.note: The strip sits above the composer, not at the top of the view; the quota warning strip (id sp-usage-warning, apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts around line 15655) uses the same placement and shows only when a usage limit is near.

items.needs: none
items.note: Searched apps/extension/src for 'pagination', 'loadMore', 'load-more', 'show more', 'hasMore' and 'cursor'; the only hit is apps/extension/src/background.ts (line 6096) returning hasMore for memories, and no side panel or options control reads it.

items.where: Side panel > first screen after signing in, with no messages yet (the empty chat)
steps: Sign in and open the side panel with a new, empty chat
Look above the message box for a greeting line (it changes with the time of day and your name)
Look at the message box placeholder
Compare with Expected: a greeting and a next step (the placeholder invites a request)
items.needs: a signed-in account and an empty chat

labels.text: How can I help you today?

items.note: When signed out the empty view shows only the AGI icon, the placeholder reads 'Sign in to chat' and the strip says 'Sign in to start chatting in Chrome.' (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts, renderEmptyGreeting around line 5868).

items.where: Open a Chrome page the extension cannot read (for example chrome://extensions) > side panel > 'Page access unavailable' card with 'Retry'
steps: Make the active tab a Chrome page such as chrome://extensions or the Chrome Web Store
Open the AGI side panel
Look at the card titled 'Page access unavailable' at the top of the messages area
Press Retry and compare with Expected: the card gives a recovery action
items.needs: a Chrome page the extension cannot read, such as chrome://extensions
items.note: The card's description text is hard-coded English in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts (sp-blocked-desc, around line 13723), not in messages.json; the card shows when the page is restricted (side_panel.ts around line 10829).

items.where: Chat composer > type @ > the list under the heading "Projects" (open tabs are listed above it); type part of a project name to narrow the list
steps: Sign in and open a chat in the side panel.
Click the message box and type @.
Look for the "Projects" heading and the project rows under it, each with "Start the chat in this project".
Type part of a project name after the @ and check that the list narrows to matches.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one project

labels.text: Start the chat in this project

items.note: The @ menu lists only open tabs and projects; I found no file or skill picker in the code, and models use the picker in S9.02.

items.where: Chat, top of the composer > model button showing "AI Assistant" (or the current model name) > "All models (n)" > type in "Search models" > click a model row
steps: Sign in and open a chat in the side panel.
Click the model button at the top of the chat.
Click "All models" and type part of a model name in "Search models".
Click a model row and check the model button now shows the model you picked.
items.needs: a signed-in account (without it the menu shows "Sign in for models")

items.where: Recent chats (clock icon in the side panel header) > "More actions" on a chat > "Move to project" > pick a project in the list labelled "Project for this chat"
steps: Sign in and click the clock icon labelled "Recent chats".
Click "More actions" on a chat row.
Click "Move to project".
Open the list "Project for this chat" and pick a project.
Check the status line "Moved to [project name]." and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one project
items.note: A second route exists: the chat title menu has "Add to project". The active project also shows as a chip "Project · NAME" in the header.

items.where: More (button in the side panel header) > "Extension settings" (opens the Permissions page) > "Browser control" menu with Auto, Ask first, Full access, YOLO
steps: Click "More" in the side panel header.
Click "Extension settings"; a new tab opens on the Permissions page.
Find "Browser control" and open its menu.
Pick "Ask first" or "Full access" and read the line under the menu.
Compare what is shown with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: No once-versus-always choice was found on this page; the closest is "Allow for this chat" on an approval card (S9.32). The background.ts line in the Code note is a scheduled-task path, not a permission choice.

items.where: More > "Shortcuts" (opens the Shortcuts page) > "Schedules" section > "New schedule" > "Repeat" menu
steps: Click "More" in the side panel header, then "Shortcuts".
In the Schedules section, click "New schedule".
Open "Repeat" and read its choices: Once, Every day, On chosen days of the week, Once a month.
Fill in the form and save; check the new schedule shows its next run time.
items.needs: none
items.note: No custom rule option is in the code; the choices are once, daily, weekly and monthly. A chat's title menu "Schedule…" also opens this form.

items.where: Chat, above an assistant reply that ran several steps: the summary line starting "Working for" or "Worked for" (click it to expand the step list)
steps: Send a request that makes AGI run several steps, such as a browser task.
While it runs, look at the summary line that starts "Working for" above the reply.
Click the summary and read the steps from top to bottom.
Compare the step order and each step's time with Expected.
items.needs: a request that runs several steps
items.note: Per-step time is shown only on tool steps; the state word appears on a step only when it was cancelled or failed.

items.needs: live-web
items.note: I searched apps/extension for board, kanban and column layouts and found none; the only task view is a list sheet opened from "Tasks".

items.where: Side panel on first open (before the tour is finished) > card "Getting started with AGI" > "Next" > "Let's go"
steps: Open the side panel for the first time, on a profile where the tour has not been finished.
Read the card titled "Getting started with AGI" and click "Next".
Read the second card and click "Let's go".
Check whether a step count or a Back button appears, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a profile where the side panel tour is not done
items.note: The tour has two cards that advance with Next; the code shows no step count and no Back button.

items.needs: none
items.note: I searched the onboarding and side panel code for an ordered setup flow; the only setup screen is a welcome page with a sign-in button and a start button, with no name or model step.

items.where: Chat, an answer that used web sources: the source chip under the answer (shows a site name, or "$SITE$ +$COUNT$" when there are several) > hover or focus it to open the source card
steps: Sign in and ask a question that needs web sources.
Find the source chip in the answer and hover over it (tap it on touch).
Read each source's title, site and excerpt in the card.
Click a source title to open it in a new tab and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a question that returns web sources (live web)
items.note: Whether a source appears depends on the answer the assistant gives.

items.where: More (button in the side panel header) > "Usage" row with a thin bar and a percent
steps: Sign in to a paid account; the Usage row is not shown on Free.
Click "More" in the side panel header.
Find the "Usage" row and read its bar and percent.
Compare the percent with Expected; the reset time is not on this row.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: The row shows only the highest window's percent. The reset time appears in the usage notice when a limit is near or reached, and the screen-reader label is "$PERCENT$% of usage budget used".

items.where: More > "Extension settings" (opens the Permissions page) > "Browser access" text, then "Browser control" and the approved-sites list
steps: Click "More" in the side panel header, then "Extension settings".
On the Permissions page, read the "Browser access" text.
Read "Browser control" and its hint about what AGI may do.
Scroll to the approved sites and blocked sites sections and compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: I did not find connected-app scopes on this page; the code covers browser sites only.

items.where: Chat, an activity summary that needs approval (it opens by itself): click the step row that says "Your approval is required before this tool can run." > "Approve" or "Decline"
steps: Send a request that makes AGI run a tool step needing approval.
Look for the activity block that opens by itself with the approval message.
Click the step row if its buttons are not visible.
Click "Approve" or "Decline" and check the recorded message and whether the run continues or stops.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a run that asks for approval

labels.text: Your approval is required before this tool can run.

items.note: The ledger had no code location; the card is in apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts (appendApprovalActions). "Allow for this chat" is a third choice on the card.

items.where: Chat, the activity summary above the reply that starts "Working for" and shows the step count; it updates while the run is active
steps: Send a request that makes AGI run a multi-step task.
Watch the summary line "Working for [time]" with its step count.
Wait and check that the time and step count change while it runs.
Click "More" then "Tasks" and check the running task's state.
items.needs: a request that runs a multi-step task
items.note: No separate latest-action field was found; the newest step is the last row when the summary is expanded.

items.where: Chat, a reply that shows a choice card (clarifying question with choices): pick answers in the card > "Send answers"
steps: Sign in and ask a question that leads AGI to offer choices.
In the card, pick one or more answers.
Click "Send answers".
Check that your answers appear as a new message in the chat.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a question that makes AGI show a choice card
items.note: The assistant decides when a card appears; there is no control to request one. Product comparison and itinerary cards are also in interactiveCards.ts.

items.where: Side panel, with focus inside it: press Command+K > type in "Search commands and chats" > Enter on a result
steps: Click inside the side panel.
Press Command+K.
Type part of a command name or chat title.
Use the arrow keys to move the highlight, then press Enter.
Check the chosen command or chat runs, and that a word with no match shows "No command or chat matches."
items.needs: none
items.note: The code accepts Command or Ctrl with K; the palette opens only when the side panel has focus.

items.needs: live-web
items.note: Searched apps/extension/src for "Create project", "New project" and "Project name" and found no create-project dialog; src/features/side-panel/activeProject.ts exists but I did not examine it.

items.where: Side panel > chat list > More actions > Delete chat
steps: Open the side panel and find a chat in the chat list.
Click the "More actions" button on that chat's row.
Click "Delete chat".

Look for the confirmation "Delete this chat from this device? It cannot be recovered." (or the account wording if the chat is saved to your AGI account) and check that nothing is removed until you confirm.
items.needs: a chat to delete (a Free account is enough)

labels.text: Delete this chat from this device? It cannot be recovered.

items.note: The confirmation text says "this chat" and does not repeat the chat's title, which Expected asks for; the confirm call in side_panel.ts passes no name. The "chat list" navigation words are my description, not a quoted label.

items.where: Scheduled task > Delete
steps: Open the scheduled task you want to remove.
Click "Delete".
Read the confirmation: "Delete $NAME$ and its run history? This cannot be undone." with the task's name in place of $NAME$.
Check that the task is still there until you confirm the deletion.
items.needs: a scheduled task to delete

labels.text: Delete $NAME$ and its run history? This cannot be undone.

items.note: I did not trace the route to the scheduled-task list, so the path before "Scheduled task" is unverified. Commands and shortcuts use a second-click confirmation ("Select delete again to remove $NAME$...", messages.json lines 1645 and 1659).

items.needs: live-web
items.note: No artifact share dialog found. Only chat sharing exists ("More actions" > "Share" > "Create link", src/side_panel.ts), which has no take-down control in the strings I read.

items.needs: live-web
items.note: Searched apps/extension/src for "publish"; hits were background publish helpers only, and no publish dialog or live-URL hand-back was found.

items.where: Add attachment > Upload from device
steps: Click the "Add attachment" button beside the message box.
Click "Upload from device".
Pick a file in the device file chooser.
Look for the picked file to appear as an attachment on the message before you send it.
items.needs: a file to upload and a signed-in AGI account (without sign-in the app says "Sign in to AGI Cloud to upload files.")
items.note: The upload option is hidden or disabled when the account's canUploadFiles capability is off.

items.where: Message box > send a message after the usage limit is reached
steps: Use an account that has used up its Managed Cloud usage.
Type a message and try to send it.
Read the notice "Your Managed Cloud usage limit has been reached."
Check for the buttons "Manage usage", "Add credits" or "Contact support", and check whether the notice shows which limit and when it resets.
items.needs: an account that has reached its usage limit

labels.text: Your Managed Cloud usage limit has been reached.

items.note: The usage code carries reset times (usageWindows.ts resetAt), but I did not confirm that the notice displays which limit or when it resets.

items.where: Microphone button > Before you dictate > Continue
steps: Click the microphone button in the message box.
Read the notice "Before you dictate" and its explanation of the microphone and Chrome's speech service.
Click "Continue" (or the decline button) and watch for Chrome's microphone prompt.
If you block access, click the microphone again and look for "Microphone access is blocked. Allow the microphone for AGI in Chrome site settings, then try again."
items.needs: a microphone, and the first-time dictation notice not yet acknowledged

labels.text: Microphone access is blocked. Allow the microphone for AGI in Chrome site settings, then try again.

items.note: The microphone button's own label was not confirmed; the notice is shown once and then stored as acknowledged.

items.where: Options > Approved sites > add a site > Grant full browser control
steps: Open the AGI extension options page.
Add a site under "Approved sites" and click the site's option to turn on browser control.
Read the explanation text, then click "Grant full browser control".
Accept Chrome's site-access prompt and check that the site now shows "browser control granted".
items.needs: a website to approve (http or https)
items.note: The control that starts consent and the exact visible heading "Approved sites" were not confirmed; the side panel's computer-use setup also reuses the same body text (computerUsePanel.ts:1590).

items.where: Side panel > computer-use task on an approved site > card "Approve action:"
steps: Start a computer-use task on a site you have approved and granted browser control.
Wait for the card titled "Approve action:" followed by the tool name.
Read the description shown on the card.
Click "Allow", "Allow for this task" or "Skip" and check that only that one call is decided.
items.needs: an approved site with browser control granted and a task that performs a browser action
items.note: Chat-level approvals use "Approve" and "Decline" (messages.json lines 1155 and 1169) and the card's "Allow" button text is in computerUsePanel.ts; I did not check which surface shows which.

items.where: Side panel > computer-use task that uploads a file > card "Approve file upload"
steps: Start a computer-use task on an approved site that needs to upload a file.
Wait for the card titled "Approve file upload" with a preview of the file.
Read the description and the file preview on the card.
Click "Allow" or "Skip" and check that the file is sent only after you allow it.
items.needs: an approved site and a file to upload
items.note: The policy has reasons for sensitive input, sensitive sites and purchases (approvalPolicy.ts), but I did not find visible text that says which outside destination the data goes to.

items.where: Options > Share crash reports
steps: Open the AGI extension options page.
Find the data-handling section that holds the "Share crash reports" toggle.
Read the description: "Crash reports stay off. Nothing is sent when an unhandled error occurs." (off) or the text about what is sent (on).
Switch the toggle on and off and check the description changes to match.
items.needs: none
items.note: The section heading for the data-handling area was not found; the toggle defaults to off (data-handling-section.ts).

items.where: Chat screen, any button or box; seen with VoiceOver
steps: Turn on VoiceOver (Command+F5).
Move VoiceOver focus to the Recent chats button at the top right of the side panel, then to the Send message button beside the message box.
Listen: each control should speak a name that says what it does.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Mac with VoiceOver
items.note: Names are set in code for many controls (aria-label in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts); the code audit did not check every control.

items.where: Chat screen and Recent chats; seen in the VoiceOver headings list
steps: Turn on VoiceOver (Command+F5).
Press VO+U, then choose Headings.
Check that the list has a top heading for the Chat panel and a heading called Recent chats.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Mac with VoiceOver
items.note: The Chat panel's top heading is a visually hidden h1 (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts). The Schedules heading on the options page is an h2 at the same level as the Shortcuts section heading (apps/extension/src/features/options/shortcuts-section.ts), so it is not nested under it.

Press Return on the More button, press Down and Up arrow keys, then press Escape.
Press Return on the Recent chats button, press Tab through the sheet, then press Escape.
Compare with Expected: all controls reachable, arrows move through the menu, Escape closes.

items.where: Side panel: Tab key from the top of the panel, starting near the message box
steps: Press Tab repeatedly from the top of the side panel.
Watch the focused control; it should show a clear outline or ring.
Check the message box placeholder and the buttons beside it.
Compare with Expected.

labels.text: How can I help you today?

Check that focus moves into the sheet: the search box or the Close recent chats button should be focused.
Press Tab repeatedly; focus should stay inside the sheet and wrap around.
Press Escape; the sheet should close. Compare with Expected.

items.where: Side panel > Recent chats (clock icon at top right)

Open Recent chats, then close it with Escape or the Close recent chats button.
Check that focus returns to the clock icon (it should show a focus ring).
Compare with Expected.

Click the message box, type a short question and press Return.

Listen while the answer streams: it should not speak each word, and it should not repeat text.
