items.where: Side panel: type in the box that says "How can I help you today?", press send, then look at the answer
steps: Type any question in the box that says "How can I help you today?" and send it.
Wait until the answer stops typing.
Compare the answer with your question: the answer is in its own bubble styled differently from your message.
Look at the small line under the answer after it finishes: it shows the model name and the time taken.
items.needs: none

labels.text: How can I help you today?

items.note: The heading "AGI said:" is screen-reader only (sp-visually-hidden), so sighted users see no name; the model name appears only after the answer finishes.

items.where: Side panel: send a question that gets a long answer with formatting
steps: Type a question that asks for a list with bold text, for example a short guide, in the box that says "How can I help you today?".
Send it and watch the answer while it is still arriving.
Check that text keeps appearing piece by piece before the answer ends.
When it ends, check that bold text, lists and code blocks are shown formatted, not as raw symbols.
items.needs: none

items.where: Side panel: send a message and look under your message before the first words arrive
steps: Type a question in the box that says "How can I help you today?" and send it.
Right after sending, look below your message for a small AGI mark with the word "Preparing".
Check that the "Preparing" line disappears once the answer text starts to appear.
Optionally, wait for the "Reading the page" wording on page-based requests (not verified how often it shows).
items.needs: none
items.note: The line sits in a role=status, aria-live=polite region, so it is announced. The mark is an image, not an animated spinner, as far as the code shows.

items.where: Side panel: send a request that makes the assistant use tools (for example a web search), then click the collapsed line above the answer that starts with "Working for" or "Worked for"
steps: Send a request that needs a tool, for example a web search about today's news.
While it works, look above the answer for a line starting with "Working for" plus the elapsed time.
Click that line to expand it.
When it finishes, check the expanded section lists the steps the assistant took, with the time and step count.
items.needs: a request that makes the assistant use tools, such as a web search
items.note: The disclosure shows steps and time, not the model's reasoning text; the "Extended thinking" toggle in the composer is a separate setting.

items.where: Side panel: after a request that used tools, expand the "Worked for" line above the answer, then click a step row
steps: Send a request that uses a tool, such as a web search.
Expand the line above the answer that starts with "Working for" or "Worked for".
Click a step row to open it.
Check the row shows what the step was, its status (for example failed or cancelled), and under it the "Request" and "Result" sections.
items.needs: a request that makes the assistant use tools, such as a web search
items.note: The row text is the step's own summary, not the raw tool name; the tool name only sets the row icon, as far as the code shows.

items.where: Side panel: ask a question that needs web sources, then look for small site-name chips inside the answer text
steps: Ask a question that needs current web information, for example a news question.
When the answer finishes, look for small link chips with a site name (for example a domain) inside the answer text.
Hover or focus one chip to see its source card.
Check that the chip opens the source page in a new tab when clicked.
items.needs: a question that makes the assistant use web sources
items.note: Chips appear only when the model returns citations; whether a given answer has them depends on the model.

items.where: Side panel: under a finished answer that used sources, click the "N sources" line to open the list
steps: Send a question that uses web sources and wait for the answer to finish.
Look under the answer for a line with a globe icon and the text "N sources".
Click that line to expand the list.
Check the list shows each source with its title, and that clicking one opens it in a new tab.
items.needs: a question that makes the assistant use web sources
items.note: The list is shown only after the answer finishes, not while it streams.

items.where: Side panel: ask the assistant to make a file (for example a text or spreadsheet file); the file card appears under the answer
steps: Send a request that asks the assistant to create a downloadable file.
When the answer finishes, look under it for a file card showing the file name and a type label (for example PDF) or the word File.
Hover the open button to see the tooltip "Open <file name>"; click it.
Hover and click the download button, labelled "Download <file name>", and check the file saves.
items.needs: a request that makes the assistant produce a file
items.note: The open and download buttons are icon-only; their words show as tooltips and screen-reader labels.

items.where: Side panel: ask for an artifact (for example a small web page); the artifact card appears under the answer, then click "Open"
steps: Send a request that asks for an artifact, for example a small web page or code file.
When the answer finishes, look under it for a card showing the artifact title and a line that starts with "Artifact".
Click the "Open" button on the card.
Check the artifact panel opens beside the chat and the button now reads "Hide"; click "Hide" to close it.
items.needs: a request that makes the assistant create an artifact
items.note: The card code is in apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/artifactPanel.ts, not generatedFiles.ts as the plan's code line says.

items.where: Side panel: ask the assistant to make an image; the image appears in the answer
steps: Send a request that asks for a picture, for example a simple drawing.
Wait for the text "Loading image…" to turn into the picture.
Click the picture to open it in the viewer.
Hover the download button, labelled "Download <file name>", and click it to save the image.
items.needs: a request that makes the assistant produce an image
items.note: If the image cannot be shown, the text is "<file name> could not be shown here. Open it instead."

items.where: Side panel: ask a question that the assistant answers with a card (for example places on a map); the card appears under the answer
steps: Send a request that returns a card, for example places near a location.
Look under the answer for a card with a headline, text and a list or buttons.
Click a card button and check it opens the link in a new tab.
In a card that cannot take input in Chrome, check the text "This card is read-only in Chrome." appears.
items.needs: a request that makes the assistant return a card

labels.text: This card is read-only in Chrome.

items.note: Which requests produce cards was not traced; the card code is in apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts.

items.where: Side panel: under a finished answer, click the copy icon button labelled "Copy response"
steps: Wait for an answer to finish.
Hover the copy icon under the answer to see the tooltip "Copy response".
Click it, then paste into a text field elsewhere.
Check the whole answer text is pasted.
items.needs: none
items.note: The button copies the raw answer text (msg.content), so markdown symbols such as ** or # may appear in the paste; on failure it shows "Could not copy. Try again."

items.where: Side panel: on the latest answer, click the icon button labelled "Try again" under it
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Hover the icon under the answer to see the tooltip "Try again".
Click it.
Check the answer is replaced by a new attempt for the same question, and that the old answer is gone.
items.needs: none for the basic button; a signed-in account for the model menu
items.note: The button appears only on the most recent answer, and not while streaming or on an error or cancelled answer.

items.where: Side panel: when an answer fails, click the "Retry" button shown under the error text
steps: Send a question in a way that makes the answer fail, for example with the internet turned off before sending.
Look under the answer for the error text and a "Retry" button.
Turn the connection back on and click "Retry".
Check the failed answer is replaced by the new outcome for the same question.
items.needs: a way to make an answer fail (for example turn off the internet before sending)
items.note: The error text comes from the failure itself, so its exact wording varies.

items.where: Side panel: on the latest answer, click the icon button labelled "Try again" to open the menu, then choose a model under "Try again with"
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Click the "Try again" icon under the answer.
If a menu opens, check it has "Try again" and the heading "Try again with" followed by model names.
Choose a different model and check a new answer for the same question appears, and the model name under it is the one you chose.
items.needs: a signed-in account, since the model list comes from the account
items.note: The menu only appears when the account has managed model options; choosing a model also changes the chat's selected model, as the code applies it.

items.where: Side panel: under a finished answer, read the small line with the model name and the time; hover it for the auto-pick reason
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Look in the action row under the answer for the model name followed by the time taken.
Hover the model name, if Auto picked the model, to see the tooltip "Auto chose this model: <reason>".
If the model was switched, look for the line "Moved to <model>: <reason>" above the action row.
items.needs: none
items.note: Token counts and cost are not shown on the answer; only the model name and time. Expected asks for tokens and cost, which the code does not display.

items.where: Side panel: make an answer fail partway through, then look at the text already shown and the error footer under it
steps: Send a question that gives a long answer.
While the text is still arriving, turn off the internet connection.
Check the text that already arrived stays on screen.
Check an error message appears under it with a "Retry" button, and that the answer is not shown as complete.
items.needs: a way to fail partway through an answer (for example losing the connection while text streams)
items.note: The incomplete mark is the error text and Retry button; there is no separate word such as "Partial" in the code.

items.where: Side panel: while an answer is still arriving, click the stop button labelled "Stop generating"
steps: Send a question that gives a long answer.
While the text is still arriving, click the stop button, whose tooltip reads "Stop generating".
Check the text that arrived stays on screen.
Check the word "Cancelled" appears under it with a "Retry" button.
items.needs: none
items.note: The expected word is "stopped", but the visible word in the code is "Cancelled".

items.where: Side panel: a turn that finishes with no text shows "No response was returned. Try again." with a "Retry" button
steps: Send a message and wait for the turn to finish.
If the reply is empty, look for the text "No response was returned. Try again." with a "Retry" button in place of an empty bubble.
Click "Retry" and check a new attempt replaces the error.
items.needs: a way to get an empty reply, which is hard to force on purpose

labels.text: No response was returned. Try again.

items.note: The code path is in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts (empty-turn check); the tester may not be able to trigger it reliably.

items.where: No control. The chat title is set from the first message you send, shown in the title row at the top of the chat and in the Recent chats list.
steps: Sign in, open a new chat and send a first message such as 'Plan a three-day trip to Lisbon'.
Look at the title row at the top of the chat.
Click the Recent chats button and find the chat in the list.

Compare the title with Expected: a meaningful title without you naming it. The code takes the first message text, collapses spaces and cuts it at 60 characters, so a long first message shows as a truncated copy of it, not a generated summary.
items.needs: none
items.note: Code derives the title from the first user message (truncated to 60 characters). It does not generate a summary title, so Expected may not match what a tester sees; the Code line's evidence lines were moved and found in conversation-history.ts, not side_panel.ts.

items.where: Recent chats > More actions for the chat > Delete chat > Delete chat (confirm)
steps: Click the Recent chats button and find the chat row.
Click the row's More actions button (its name is 'More actions for' the chat title), then click Delete chat.

Read the confirmation: 'Delete this chat from this device? It cannot be recovered.' (or, for a chat synced to your account, '...from this device and from your AGI account?'). Click Delete chat to confirm, or Cancel to stop.
Look for the status 'Chat deleted.' and check the chat is gone from Recent chats and from the title row.
items.needs: none for a chat saved only on this device; a signed-in account with a synced chat for the account wording and the 'disappears everywhere' check; a second signed-in device to see the chat is gone there
items.note: The confirmation is in place (confirmHistoryAction); the Code line's quoted lines moved, but the delete path is at side_panel.ts around line 12661 and the menu items around 12771 and 12801.

items.where: Model button in the message box (the button showing the model name) > AGI Work switch
steps: Open a chat and send one message.
Click the model button in the message box, the one that shows the model name.
Turn on the switch labelled AGI Work. Its description reads 'Plans and runs multi-step tasks with tools and files...'.
Send a multi-step request, then check that the model button shows an 'AGI Work' badge and that later messages in this chat use it. Turn the switch off and check the badge goes away.
items.needs: a plan that includes AGI Work (otherwise the row is shown locked with 'available on' text)

labels.text: Later messages in this chat use it until you turn it off.

items.note: The only mode in this code is AGI Work on or off; there is no separate agent or plan mode switch. Starting a new chat resets the mode to chat (side_panel.ts around lines 1827 and 1965).

items.where: Add attachment button > Temporary chat
steps: Start a new, empty chat. Click the Add attachment button in the message box.
Click Temporary chat. Hover over it first to read its tooltip, which explains what is not saved.
Look for the banner: 'Temporary chat. Stays out of your history, search, memory and Library.'

Send a message, then click Add attachment again and click Temporary chat. Check the prompt offers End temporary chat, End and discard, Keep chatting or Turn off, and that after ending the chat is absent from Recent chats.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Stays out of your history, search, memory and Library.

items.note: The Temporary chat item is hidden once a chat has messages, so it can only be turned on in an empty chat (startTemporaryChat returns early when messages exist). The Expected example names 'incognito' and 'local-only'; the code has only Temporary chat, with no local-only mode.

items.where: Chat title row > More actions for the chat > Continue on phone
steps: Open a chat that is saved to your account (signed in, account mirroring on).
Click the More actions button on the chat title row, then click Continue on phone.
A sheet titled 'Continue on your phone' shows a code and the text 'Scan this code with your phone's camera to open this chat in AGI.' Use Copy link to copy the link.
On the other device, sign in with the same account, open the link or scan the code, and check the same chat opens.
items.needs: a signed-in account, a chat synced to the account (the item only appears for chats with a cloud conversation), and a second device signed in with the same account
items.note: The item is not shown for chats saved only on this device, and Account mirroring off in AGI settings keeps chats local; the Code evidence lines (background.ts ~6167, side_panel.ts ~599) are the sync and status code, not the menu item itself.

items.where: Open the AGI side panel in Chrome, then in the composer (placeholder "How can I help you today?") type a message and press the send button
steps: Open the AGI side panel in Chrome.
Type any short message in the composer and press send.
Look at the answer area right after pressing send and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account

labels.text: How can I help you today?

items.note: The code has no separate 'accepted' wording. The first visible state after send is the 'Preparing' indicator, which is set when the send starts.

items.where: Open the AGI side panel, send a message, then type and send a second message while the first answer is still streaming
steps: Send a message that gets a long answer.
While it is still answering, type a second message.
Look at the composer placeholder and the queued list above it: the second message should show as queued with Edit and Cancel.
items.needs: a signed-in account

labels.text: Reply to send it after this answer

items.note: The queued row reads 'Queued: <your text>' and, with more than one, 'Queued 1 of 2' style numbering.

items.where: Open the AGI side panel, attach or use the current page as context, then send a message
steps: Open a normal web page and open the AGI side panel.
Send a message that uses the page as context.
Look for the thinking label before the answer starts.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a normal web page open
items.note: 'Reading the page' is set when page context is read (side_panel.ts setThinkingLabel); attachment-only preparation may show only 'Preparing'.

items.where: Open the AGI side panel and ask a question that needs browsing history, for example 'What did I read about X yesterday?'
steps: Ask a question that needs the browsing history.
Watch the step row under the answer while it works.
Look for 'Searching browsing history' and, when sources are used, 'Sources for <query>'.
items.needs: a signed-in account and browsing-history access granted to the extension
items.note: The query text is shown only when the activity carries one. The exact trigger depends on the model deciding to search, so it is not always reproducible.

items.where: Open the AGI side panel and ask for something that makes the assistant run code, for example 'Use code to add 1234 and 5678'
steps: Send a request that needs code to be run.
Watch the answer while the code step is running.
Look for the 'Running code…' label, then the finished code block.
items.needs: a signed-in account; code execution must be available on the chosen route
items.note: The label is shown in the code execution block (bubbles.ts). Whether code runs depends on the route.

items.where: Open the AGI side panel, ask for something that uses a connected service, then open the activity row under the answer ('Working for <time>') and expand the step
steps: Connect a service in the AGI account and ask for something that uses it.
While it works, open the activity row under the answer.
Expand the step and look for the service name in the step summary and the 'Request' heading while the call is in progress.
items.needs: a connected service (connector or MCP tool) and a signed-in account
items.note: The service name comes from the server's step summary, not a fixed label, so the exact words depend on the service. Where the connector is set up was not traced.

items.where: Open the AGI side panel and send a request that needs a tool approval; in the activity row under the answer, expand the step with 'Needs your approval · <time>'
steps: Send a request that needs a tool approval.
Open the activity row labelled 'Needs your approval · <time>' under the answer.
Expand the step and look for the approval text with the Approve and Decline buttons, and for the 'Allow for this chat' choice.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a tool that needs approval

labels.text: Your approval is required before this tool can run.

items.note: 'Allow for this chat' is hidden for high-risk approvals (bubbles.ts).

items.where: Open the AGI side panel and send a request where the assistant needs information; the activity row under the answer shows 'Needs your input · <time>' and an input form
steps: Send a request that needs a detail from you.
Open the activity row labelled 'Needs your input · <time>'.
Expand the step and look for the '<server> needs your input' heading and the form with a Submit button.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a connector that asks for input
items.note: The input form is built in apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/connectorInputForm.ts.

items.where: Visible in the answer area: the 'Preparing' indicator is replaced by the answer text
steps: Send any message.
Watch the 'Preparing' indicator under the composer.
Look for it to disappear as soon as the first answer text appears.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: There is no control for this. The thinking indicator is removed when the first content arrives (side_panel.ts removeThinking).

items.where: Visible in the answer bubble while the model is answering
steps: Send a message that gets a long answer.
Watch the answer bubble while it is still answering.
Look for the text to grow line by line instead of appearing all at once.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: A rendering behaviour with no control of its own.

items.where: Visible in the answer bubble while the model is answering
steps: Ask for an answer that has a list, a table and a code block.
Watch the answer while it is still streaming.
Look for the list, table and code block to render correctly before the answer finishes.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: A rendering behaviour with no control of its own. Whether the model produces a table depends on the answer.

items.where: Click 'Recent chats' in the side panel, then look at the badge on each chat row
steps: Send a message and wait for the answer to finish.
Click the 'Recent chats' button in the side panel.
Look at the badge on the chat row: 'Syncing to your account' while it saves, then 'Saved to your account'; for a browser-only chat it says 'Saved on this device'.
items.needs: a signed-in account for the account copy; without it only 'Saved on this device' appears
items.note: The save status is a badge on the Recent chats list, not inside the answer. The tooltip text is in the same code.

items.where: Send a request that uses steps (for example a browser or tool step); when it ends, the activity row under the answer reads 'Worked for <time>'
steps: Send a request that uses at least one tool or browser step.
Wait for the answer to finish.
Look at the activity row under the answer: it should read 'Worked for <time>' and the streaming indicator should stop.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a request that uses steps
items.note: There is no separate 'Completed' word. A plain answer with no steps may show no activity row.

items.where: Send a request where one step fails but others succeed; the activity row under the answer reads 'Finished with errors · <time>'
steps: Send a request with several steps where one is expected to fail.
Wait for the run to finish.
Look at the activity row: 'Finished with errors · <time>', or 'Worked for <time>' with failed attempts, which is distinct from 'Worked for' alone.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a run where some steps fail
items.note: Getting a partial run on demand is hard; the failed-attempts text is a plural key (_one and _other).

items.where: Send a message, then while the answer is streaming press the send button, which now reads 'Stop generating'
steps: Send a message that gets a long answer.
While it is still streaming, press the button labelled 'Stop generating'.
Look at the button and the answer: it should show 'Stopping…' and stay disabled until the stop takes effect.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The 'Stopping…' text also appears in the bubble status while the stop is pending.

items.where: Stop a running answer with 'Stop generating'; the activity row under the answer reads 'Cancelled after <time>'
steps: Send a message with steps, then press 'Stop generating' while it runs.
Wait until the stop takes effect.
Look at the activity row: 'Cancelled after <time>', and check the text that already arrived is still shown.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: A plain streamed answer without steps may not show the activity row.

items.where: Send a message, then lose the connection while it is answering; the bubble shows 'Reconnecting…'
steps: Send a message that gets a long answer.
Turn off the network connection briefly while it is answering, then turn it back on.
Look for the 'Reconnecting…' status in the answer bubble, and check the answer continues when the connection returns.
items.needs: a signed-in account and the ability to drop the connection
items.note: Reconnecting is set for cloud runs (side_panel.ts); the exact drop method is up to the tester.

items.where: Close and reopen the AGI side panel while an answer is still running; the bubble shows 'Reconnecting…' and resumes
steps: Send a message that gets a long answer.
Close the side panel while it is still answering.
Reopen the side panel and look at the answer: it should show 'Reconnecting…' and keep going, not start over.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: No separate 'Resuming' word exists in the code; the same 'Reconnecting…' label is used while the run is picked up again.

items.where: Send a message on a model that is rate limited; the answer bubble shows 'The model is busy right now.' with a 'Try again in <time>.' line when a wait is known
steps: Send a message on a model that is rate limited.
Wait for the error in the answer bubble.
Look for 'The model is busy right now.' and the 'Try again in' time, and the Retry button.
items.needs: a model with a rate limit at the time of the test

labels.text: The model is busy right now.

items.note: The wait time comes from the server. Making a rate limit happen on demand is not controllable from the app.

items.where: Send a message when the account's usage allowance is used up; the answer bubble shows the limit text with an 'Upgrade' button (also 'Add credits' or 'Manage usage' when offered)
steps: Use up the usage allowance on a Free account, or use an account with an exhausted limit.
Send a message.
Look for the limit text in the answer bubble and the 'Upgrade' button below it, and check it leads to the upgrade or usage page.
items.needs: a Free account with its allowance used up, or an account with an exhausted limit

labels.text: The free model has used up the allowance everyone on the Free plan shares, so this is not a limit on your account.

items.note: Which copy appears depends on whether the limit is the shared free pool, a spending cap or the account allowance.

items.where: Send a message after your sign-in has expired; the panel shows 'Sign in to use AGI Cloud chat.' with a 'Sign in' button
steps: Let the sign-in expire, or sign out in the AGI account, then open the side panel.
Send a message.
Look for the error text 'Sign in to AGI Cloud to send messages.' and the 'Sign in' button that offers to sign in again.
items.needs: a signed-in account whose sign-in can be expired

labels.text: Sign in to use AGI Cloud chat.
Sign in to AGI Cloud to send messages.

items.note: The answer bubble itself shows only the error text and a Retry button; the 'Sign in' offer is the gate above the composer.

items.where: Send a request that needs your desktop (or a paired device) while that device is offline; the activity row shows 'Waiting for your desktop · <time>' or 'Waiting for <device> · <time>'
steps: Turn off the paired device or desktop app.
Send a request that needs it.
Open the activity row under the answer and look for 'Waiting for your desktop' or 'Waiting for <device>', and in the step 'Waiting for <device> to run this step.'
items.needs: a paired device that can be turned off

labels.text: Waiting for $DEVICE$ to run this step.

items.note: The device name comes from the step.

items.where: Send a message when the chosen model is unavailable; the answer bubble shows the error with 'Retry' and 'Switch model' buttons
steps: Send a message on a model that is unavailable (for example a retired or down model).
Wait for the error in the answer bubble.
Look for 'The model is not available right now.' or 'The selected model is not available.', then the 'Retry' and 'Switch model' buttons.
items.needs: a model that is unavailable at the time of the test

labels.text: The model is not available right now. Try again in a moment.
The selected model is not available. It may have been retired. Choose another model, or switch to Auto.

items.note: The exact sentence depends on whether Auto chose the model.

items.where: Send a message with an attachment too large for the model, or a very long chat; the answer bubble explains what to change
steps: Attach a file that is too large, or keep a chat until it is too long for the model.
Send the message.

Look for 'An attachment is too large for the selected model.' or 'This conversation is too long for the selected model.' and the suggested fix, then check you can change it and send again with the Retry button.
items.needs: a file too large for the model, or a very long conversation

labels.text: An attachment is too large for the selected model. Remove or shrink it, or choose a model with larger media limits.
This conversation is too long for the selected model. Start a new chat, remove some attachments, or choose a model with a larger context window.
$FILE$ was not added. Attachments must total under $LIMIT$.

items.note: The attachment size check in the composer shows the second label before sending.

items.where: Send a message, let some answer text arrive, then make the answer fail; the partial text stays with the error and a 'Retry' button below it
steps: Send a message that starts to answer.
Cause a failure after some text has arrived (for example lose the connection and keep it off).
Look at the answer: the text that arrived should still be there, with the error text and the 'Retry' button under it.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a way to fail mid-answer
items.note: Code keeps the content and sets the error footer (chat-state.ts, bubbles.ts); a forced mid-answer failure is hard to produce on demand.

items.where: Recent chats (clock button in the side panel header) > click the chat's row
steps: Sign in, start a chat, send a message and let the answer finish.
Send a second message and press the stop button while the answer is still arriving, so that turn ends stopped.
Close the side panel and quit Chrome completely, then open Chrome again and open the AGI side panel.
Click the clock button whose tooltip is Recent chats, then click the chat's row.
Compare with Expected: the earlier answer and the partial stopped answer are both there, and the stopped turn shows its Cancelled footer.
items.needs: an account (signed in) and a Chrome restart
items.note: The code restores the latest stored chat on launch (side_panel.ts resumeLatestStoredManagedRun), but I did not confirm from the code that the panel always reopens that chat by itself, so the tester should open it from Recent chats; the interrupted footer text Cancelled comes from agentTaskStateLabel in packages/contracts/types/src/cross-device.ts, not from the extension files.

items.where: More (the three-dot button in the side panel header) > Tasks
steps: Sign in and start a task that runs for a while, such as a Cloud agent run from the composer.
Close the side panel while the task is still running.
Wait a minute, then open the AGI side panel again.
Click the More button, then click Tasks.

items.where: Chat screen: + (attach button) > Upload from device, then type the question in the message box and send
steps: Click the + button next to the message box and click Upload from device.
Choose one PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF image in the file chooser.
Type a question about the picture, for example: What is in this picture?
Press Enter to send.
Look at the reply: it should describe or answer about the image you attached, as Expected says.

items.where: Chat screen: + (attach button) > Upload from device, pick several files, then send
steps: Click the + button and click Upload from device.

Check that each image appears as a thumbnail above the message box.
Type a question such as: What is different between these two pictures?
Press Enter and look at the reply: it should compare all the images you attached.

items.note: One message takes at most 5 files (MANAGED_CHAT_MAX_ATTACHMENTS in apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/managedChatHandler.ts), and the selected model may accept fewer images; the notice reads that the model accepts one image, or up to a count, per message (apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json). items.where: Chat screen: + (attach button) > Take a screenshot, or paste a screenshot into the message box

Click the + button and click Take a screenshot.
Or copy a screenshot to the clipboard and press Cmd+V in the message box.
Type a question such as: What does this screenshot show?
Press Enter and look at the reply: it should explain what is in the captured image, as Expected says.
items.needs: a normal website open in the current tab; a screenshot on the clipboard for the paste route
items.note: If the tab cannot be captured the app says: To capture this tab, click the extension icon in Chrome’s toolbar, then try again (apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json). Dragging an image onto the composer is a third route (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts). The screenshot item is disabled when uploads are off for the account.

items.where: Side panel > composer at the bottom of the chat > microphone button labelled "Voice input"
steps: Sign in and open the side panel on a chat.
Find the small microphone icon button in the composer bar, next to the message field. Its accessible name is "Voice input".
Click it. If a "Before you dictate" notice appears, click "Continue", then allow the microphone in Chrome's prompt.
Look for the button to pulse and its tooltip to change to "Listening… click to stop". Speak a short sentence.
Click the microphone again to stop. Compare: the spoken words should appear as text in the message field.

items.note: Code pointers moved: the quoted lines are gone, but setupVoiceInput in src/features/side-panel/voice.ts and the wiring at src/side_panel.ts (setupVoiceInput call near line 15826) hold the feature.

items.where: Side panel > composer at the bottom of the chat > microphone button labelled "Voice input"
steps: Start dictation with the "Voice input" microphone button in the composer bar.
Speak a sentence, then click the microphone again to stop.
Compare: the transcript is added to the message field and is not sent to the chat.
Click inside the message field and type or delete a word to edit the transcript.
Compare: the edit stays in the field until you press send yourself.
items.needs: a microphone and Chrome microphone permission
items.note: Code reads the transcript into the textarea through appendComposerText (src/features/side-panel/composerText.ts); nothing in voice.ts sends it. Whether it is sent is not checked here.

items.where: Side panel > More button > "Extension settings" (opens the options page) > left navigation "Options" > "Dictation" row, select box below it
steps: Open the side panel and click the "More" button.
Click "Extension settings". A settings tab opens.
In the left navigation, click "Options". Scroll down to the "Dictation" row.
Open the select box in that row and pick a different language.
Compare: the status line "Dictation language saved." appears. Then open the side panel, click "Voice input" and check its tooltip shows the new language name.
items.needs: none (a microphone only to test that recognition uses the chosen language)

labels.text: The microphone transcribes in this language. The list is the languages this browser is set up for; add more in Chrome's language settings.

items.note: The choices come from the Chrome profile's languages, so the list only grows by adding languages in Chrome settings. The select sits in the "Options" section (src/features/options/preference-rows.ts), not in the composer; the More button's placement was not verified visually.

items.where: Side panel > composer at the bottom of the chat > microphone button labelled "Voice input"
steps: Click the "Voice input" microphone button and wait for it to pulse.
Speak a full sentence, then click the microphone again to stop.
Compare: the final transcript appears in the message field once dictation ends.
Click the microphone, stay silent until it stops by itself.
Compare: the notice "No speech was heard. Try again and speak after the button starts pulsing." appears above the composer.
items.needs: a microphone and Chrome microphone permission

labels.text: No speech was heard. Try again and speak after the button starts pulsing.

items.note: Only one final result is used (interimResults is false), and the text is added when the recognizer returns it, so the field may update only after you stop speaking. Code pointers moved: see voice.ts onresult and onend handlers.

items.where: Side panel > composer at the bottom of the chat > microphone button "Voice input" > then click into the message field and press Command+Z
steps: Dictate a sentence with the "Voice input" microphone button and stop it.
Click into the message field so it has focus.
Press Command+Z (the browser's normal undo).
Compare: the dictated text is removed. Press Command+Z again to check that earlier typing is handled normally.
items.needs: a microphone and Chrome microphone permission
items.note: Insertion uses document.execCommand('insertText') in src/features/side-panel/composerText.ts, which normally keeps the browser undo stack; the fallback path sets the field value directly and may not be undoable. Not verified in a running browser.

items.where: No control of its own. The effect shows in a chat reply in the AGI Chrome side panel, when the prompt matches a skill's description.
steps: Make sure the account has skills of its own or in the catalog, and that the workspace allows skills.
Open the AGI side panel and send a request that closely matches the description of one skill, without choosing a skill in the Attach menu (the Skills entry, labelled "Skills", must stay unchecked).
Look at the reply: it should use the matching skill's behaviour, as the skill would be applied without being asked. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account, plus a skill whose description matches the request
items.note: The auto-match runs on the server, not in apps/extension: applyImplicitManagedSkillOffer and selectOfferedSkills (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:1082 and :5442, skill-offer.ts) add relevant skills to the system prompt on every surface except vscode, cli and api, so chrome is included. The extension only sends an explicit skillName chosen by hand (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:15157-15180). The side panel does not show any message that a skill was matched, and I did not confirm how the result is labelled in the reply. The Code line's side_panel.ts:6916 points at unrelated keepalive code, and the freeTrialClient.ts:825 quote could not be found; neither affects this item.

items.where: Side panel > Plus menu (+) > Connectors to connect an app (it opens the connector directory on the web). Then ask a question that uses the connected app, and read the step row under the answer.
steps: Open the AGI side panel and sign in.
Click the plus (+) button and choose Connectors, which opens the connector directory on the web; connect an app there, then return to the side panel.
In the side panel, send a question that needs the connected app's data.
Wait for the answer, then open or look at the activity steps shown with it.
Look for a step that reads "Using <app name> connector" and confirm it names the app that supplied the data, as Expected says.
items.needs: a connected connector (set up from Plus menu > Connectors); an outside account for that app
items.note: The name comes from a server-side template in tool-loop.ts that shows as an activity step summary (rendered in bubbles.ts); the code does not show the answer text itself naming the provider. Without a display name the step reads "Using connector". The bubbles.ts:844 line is the search-sources step ("Sources for $QUERY$"), not a connector attribution. The exact step location in the side panel was not confirmed as a visible heading.

Click "More" > "Tasks" to see runs, and compare with Expected.

items.where: Chat > ask a question that uses a tool > under the answer, click "Worked for …" and read the step line

items.where: Chat > ask a question that uses a tool > under the answer, click "Worked for …" > click a tool step row

a chat where the assistant ran a tool with a long result
items.note: Code found: the result is kept in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-result-store.ts and the reader is the model-facing tool read_tool_result (tool-result-store.ts:12). Its reference appears in the model's context notice, and the extension (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts:1065) has no control or wording for reading a stored result. items.where: Side panel chat > the assistant's tool step (its summary row) > tap the row to expand it > read the 'Request' and 'Result' headings

steps: Open the side panel and click the "Computer Use" tab.

items.where: No control of its own. Seen in the Computer Use tab of the side panel: run a browser task, change the page state, then have the assistant discover tools again and compare the activity log.
steps: Open the side panel and click the "Computer Use" tab.

items.needs: A Free or paid account, and a site whose WebMCP tool set changes with page state. The repo has no such test site.

labels.text: Discover tools supplied by this website.

The cited lines (agentLoop.ts:636, background.ts:4326) no longer hold the quoted code; the current handling is in webmcp.ts (watchForToolChanges) and background.ts around lines 2279-2314.
