Approval appears inline only in the chat activity line (spActivityNeedsApproval), outside the overview. Searched apps/extension for unblock, approve and awaiting_input.

items.where: More (⋮) > Tasks > Open
steps: Sign in to AGI in the side panel and have at least one task in your history.
Click the ⋮ button at the top of the side panel, then click Tasks.
On a task row, click Open (or open the row named 'Open task: <title>').

Look at the opened page: it is the web chat for that task, showing its full transcript. Compare with Expected (full transcript drill-down from the overview). Note it opens in a browser tab on the web, not inside the side panel.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one task
items.note: Open goes to the web chat page (/chat/<id>) rather than showing the transcript inside the extension (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/tasksSheet.ts).

items.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > New schedule
steps: Open the side panel and click More, then Shortcuts (this opens the Options page on the Shortcuts section).
Under Schedules, click New schedule.
Type a Name and write the instructions in Instructions.
Pick a Repeat option, fill in the Time, and click Create schedule.
Compare: a message 'Created <name>. It runs in the cloud even when this browser is closed.' appears and the new routine is listed in Schedules.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account
items.note: A second route exists: the chat title's More actions menu has 'Schedule…', which opens Shortcuts with the form pre-filled from the chat's first prompt.

items.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > (routine row) Edit
steps: Open More, then Shortcuts, and find the routine in Schedules.
Click Edit on that routine row.
Change the Name, and type or clear the Description (optional) field.
Click Save changes.
Compare: the message 'Saved <name>.' appears and the row shows the new name and description; Edit again shows the saved values.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account and one saved routine

items.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > (routine row) Edit > Instructions
steps: Open More, then Shortcuts, and click Edit on a routine.
Click inside the Instructions box.
Type several lines, pressing Return between them.
Click Save changes, then click Edit again.
Compare: the Instructions box is a multi-line box that keeps all the lines you typed.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account and one saved routine

items.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > New schedule > Repeat
steps: Open More, then Shortcuts, then click New schedule.
Fill in Name and Instructions.
Open Repeat and choose Every day (or On chosen days of the week, or Once a month), then fill in Time.
Click Create schedule.
Compare: the routine row shows 'Next <time>' matching the cadence you chose. Whether a run starts at each occurrence is decided on the server and can only be seen later in Runs.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account; waiting past a scheduled time to see a run

labels.text: On chosen days of the week

items.note: The Repeat options in code are Once, Every day, On chosen days of the week and Once a month.

items.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > (routine row) Run now
steps: Open More, then Shortcuts, and find a routine in Schedules.
Click Run now on its row.
Compare: the message 'Run started.' appears.
Click Runs on the same row and wait for the new run to show a final status.
Compare: the run is listed with status Finished or Failed and its output text.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account and one saved routine

items.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > (routine row)
steps: Open More, then Shortcuts, and scroll to Schedules.
Read the line 'Next <time>' on each routine row.
Compare the time with the schedule you set in Repeat and Time.
Create a routine with a future time and check that its row shows the new Next time.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account and one saved routine
items.note: The Next line is only added to the row when a next time exists.

items.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > (routine row)
steps: Open More, then Shortcuts, and find a routine in Schedules.
Read the line 'Last <time>' or 'Not run yet' on its row.
If a run failed, read the 'Last run: <error>' line under it.
Compare with the Runs list: the newest run's time and status should match the row.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account; a routine that has run (a failed run shows the error line)
items.note: The status badge on the row shows the raw status word from the data (for example 'failed'), not a translated label.

items.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > (routine row) Runs
steps: Open More, then Shortcuts, and click Runs on a routine row that has run.
Read the run list under the heading Runs.
For each run, read its status (Finished, Failed and so on) and the output text under it.
Compare: each run shows its output text, not only its status.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account and a routine that has run at least once

items.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > (routine row) Pause
steps: Open More, then Shortcuts, and find a routine in Schedules.
Click Pause on its row.
Compare: the message 'Schedule paused.' appears and the button changes to Resume; the routine stays in the list.
Click Resume.
Compare: the message 'Schedule resumed.' appears and the button changes back to Pause.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account and one saved routine

items.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > (routine row) Delete
steps: Open More, then Shortcuts, and click Delete on a routine row.
Read the confirmation 'Delete <name> and its run history? This cannot be undone.'
Click Cancel first and check the routine is still listed.
Click Delete again, then Delete in the confirmation.
Compare: the message 'Deleted <name>.' appears and the routine is gone from the list.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account and one saved routine you can afford to delete

labels.text: Delete $NAME$ and its run history? This cannot be undone.

items.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > (routine row with a waiting run)
steps: Open More, then Shortcuts, and find a routine whose run is waiting for approval.
Read the block 'Paused until you approve or deny this step' with its expiry line and the action it asks for.
Click Approve (or Deny).
Compare: the message 'Approved. The run continued.' (or 'Denied. The run continued without that step.') appears, the waiting block goes away, and the run reaches a final status under Runs.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account and a routine whose unattended run reaches a tool call that needs approval

labels.text: Paused until you approve or deny this step

items.note: The code does not name a simple user action that triggers an approval; the approval comes from the tool-call gate during an unattended run, so the tester may need a routine whose run calls a tool that requires approval.

items.where: Chat tab > + (Add attachment) > Add the browser page
steps: Open a normal website in a tab and open the side panel (toolbar AGI icon).
In the Chat tab, click the + button labelled Add attachment, then click Add the browser page.
Type a question that depends on the page, such as what the page says about a named topic, and send it.
Check the answer uses the content of the open page, and that the page chip shows the site's host.
items.needs: a normal website tab open
items.note: The site may first ask for access with a card 'AGI needs access to <host>' (Allow for this task, Always allow on this site, Decline).

items.where: Chat tab > + (Add attachment) > Add selected text
steps: On a normal website, highlight a sentence or paragraph with the mouse.
Open the side panel and click the + button labelled Add attachment.
Click Add selected text, then type a question about the highlighted text and send it.
Check the answer refers to the highlighted text.
items.needs: a normal website and the site approved in Extension settings
items.note: If the site is not approved the notice reads 'Approve <host> in Extension settings to add text selected there.' Right-clicking a selection also offers 'Explain this' and 'Translate this' in apps/extension/src/background.ts.

items.where: Right-click page background > Summarize this page
steps: Open a normal website and right-click an empty part of the page (not a link, image or text).
Click Summarize this page in the menu.
The side panel opens with the page attached; wait for the reply.
Check the reply summarizes the page that is open in the tab.
items.needs: a normal website tab

items.where: Website tab > Ask AGI launcher (round button at the edge of the page) > text box 'Ask one question about this page…'
steps: Open a website that you have approved for AGI, and make sure the side panel is closed (the launcher hides while it is open).
Click the round Ask AGI launcher button on the page.
Type a question about the page into the box labelled Ask one question about this page… and press Enter.
Check the streamed answer uses the visible text of this page.
items.needs: an approved website and the Page assistant overlay setting on

labels.text: Ask one question about this page…

items.note: The overlay mounts only on approved origins when the setting is on (apps/extension/src/inPagePanel/setup.ts). Its default state was not found in the code. The Options page setting is in the Options section (apps/extension/src/features/options/preference-rows.ts).

items.where: YouTube watch page > Ask AGI launcher > Summarize video, Key timestamps or Q&A
steps: Open a YouTube video that has captions, on an approved site.
Click the Ask AGI launcher on the page.
Click the chip Summarize video (or Key timestamps, or Q&A).
Wait for 'Reading the video captions…', then check the answer is about what is said in the video.
items.needs: a YouTube video with captions
items.note: Typed questions in the box send the visible page text, not the transcript (apps/extension/src/features/content/in-page-panel/panel.ts submitComposer); only the three video chips read captions. Videos without captions get a 'no captions' reply.

items.where: Toolbar AGI icon (or Open AGI side panel shortcut) > Chat tab
steps: Open the side panel with the toolbar AGI icon, or the shortcut Command+Shift+K on Mac.
In the Chat tab, ask a question and wait for the answer.
Switch to a different website tab and come back to the side panel.
Check the same conversation is still shown, then click New chat and check a new empty conversation starts.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account
items.note: The shortcut is set in the manifest (apps/extension/manifest.json) and can be changed in Chrome's shortcut page.

items.where: Computer Use tab > Task > Start
steps: Open a normal website tab and open the side panel, then click the Computer Use tab.
If the panel asks, click the Allow browser control button for the site.
Type in the Task box a goal such as 'Open https://example.com' and click Start.
Check the tab goes to that address and the Assistant steps list shows the opening step.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account and an approved site
items.note: No separate Open URL control was found; the navigate tool is used inside a Computer Use task. Only http and https addresses are allowed.

items.where: Computer Use tab > Task > Start
steps: Open a website that has its own search box and open the Computer Use tab.
In the Task box type a goal such as 'Search this site for a term and read me the first three results', then click Start.
Watch the Assistant steps list as the search is typed and submitted.
Check the reply reads back the results shown on the page.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account and an approved site
items.note: No separate search control was found; website search is done as a Computer Use task.

items.where: Computer Use tab > Run Autofill (job application pages), or Computer Use tab > Task > Start (other forms)
steps: Open a job application form on an approved site (Greenhouse, Lever or Ashby for Run Autofill).
Open the Computer Use tab and click Run Autofill.
For another form, type in the Task box a goal such as 'Fill the name and email fields with the details I give you' and click Start.
Check the fields show the values that were asked for, and that password and payment fields were left alone.
items.needs: a web form and a signed-in AGI account

items.where: Computer Use tab > Task > Start
steps: Open a website with several linked pages and open the Computer Use tab.
In the Task box type a goal with several steps, such as 'Find the contact phone number on this site, then open the pricing page and read the first price', and click Start.
Watch the Steps counter (Steps: n/max) and the Assistant steps list climb over several actions.
Check the run ends with an 'Agent finished' entry and the answer covers both parts of the goal.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account and an approved site

items.where: Computer Use tab > Task > Start, on a website that declares its own tools
steps: Open a website that publishes WebMCP tools (none is named in the code, so find one first).
In the Computer Use tab type a task the site's tool can do, and click Start.
Check Assistant steps shows a call to the site's tool rather than only clicks.
For a tool that changes data, check the page shows a confirmation dialog that must be accepted before the call runs.
items.needs: a website that declares WebMCP tools
items.note: The agent's tools discover_site_tools and call_site_tool are in apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/browserToolDefinitions.ts. Whether the agent picks a site tool is its choice, and the write-tool dialog is window.confirm in apps/extension/src/webmcp.ts.

items.where: Computer Use tab > Assistant steps
steps: Start any Computer Use task (see Task and Start).
While it runs, click the Assistant steps toggle to open the list.
Watch each action appear as it happens, with its time.
Check the list matches the actions the tab takes, and the last entry is the final report.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account and an approved site

items.where: Computer Use tab > Assistant steps > Screenshot captured
steps: Start a Computer Use task and open Assistant steps.
Watch the browser tab itself, which is the task's visible page.
When an entry titled 'Screenshot captured' appears, click its thumbnail to view it larger.
Check the thumbnail shows the current state of the page.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account and an approved site
items.note: The code shows screenshot thumbnails added as the agent takes them, not a continuous live stream. The live view is the Chrome tab the task runs in.

items.where: Chrome tab strip: during a Computer Use run the tab is put in a blue tab group titled AGI
steps: Open a normal website tab that is not already in a Chrome tab group.
Start a Computer Use task on that tab (Computer Use tab > Task > Start).
Look at the Chrome tab strip for a blue group titled AGI around that tab.
After the run ends, check the tab has left the group.
items.needs: none
items.note: A tab already in a Chrome tab group is not regrouped (apps/extension/src/background.ts markComputerUseTab). The right-click item Add Tab to AGI Group is a separate manual control.

items.where: Computer Use tab > Task > Start, on a site that asks you to sign in during the task
steps: Start a Computer Use task on a site that needs you to sign in (for example a site with a login page).
Wait for the banner titled 'Your turn' to appear.
Click Take over, sign in on the page, then click Continue.
Check AGI carries on with the task after Continue and the run reaches Agent finished.
items.needs: a site that asks you to sign in during a task, a signed-in AGI account, an approved site
items.note: The hand-off is requested by the agent's ask_user_to_take_over tool (apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/agentLoop.ts). The Take over and Continue controls are the same ones used here.

items.where: Computer Use tab > Task > Start, on a page that shows a CAPTCHA or human check
steps: Start a Computer Use task on a page that shows a CAPTCHA or 'I am not a robot' check.
Wait for the banner titled 'Your turn' to appear.
Click Take over, solve the check on the page, then click Continue.
Check AGI resumes the task after Continue.
items.needs: a page that shows a CAPTCHA or human check, a signed-in AGI account, an approved site
items.note: The agent is told never to solve a CAPTCHA itself (apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/agentLoop.ts).

items.where: Computer Use tab > Stop (shown while a run is active), or Take over
steps: Start a Computer Use task that takes several actions.
While it runs, click Stop, or click Take over to pause AGI.
Check the Stop control changes to Stopping… and the run ends.
Check a banner titled 'Browser control stopped' appears and no more actions happen on the page.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account and an approved site

items.where: Computer Use tab > Task > Start, on a page that offers a file to download
steps: Start a Computer Use task that downloads a file from a page.
Before the download, check an approval card appears titled 'Approve action: download_file'.
Read the card, then click Allow or Skip.
Check the step 'Download: <address>' is listed in Assistant steps.
items.needs: a page that offers a file to download
items.note: Downloads are always asked for (apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/approvalPolicy.ts). The code shows the approval card and the step list; no separate downloads list was found.

items.where: Computer Use tab > Task > Start, on a page with a file upload control
steps: Have a small file ready on the computer.
Start a Computer Use task that needs to upload that file to a page.
When the card 'Approve file upload' appears, click Choose files to upload and pick the file. Check the preview lists it and nothing has been sent yet.
Click Allow to send it, or Skip, and check the result shown in Assistant steps.
items.needs: a file to upload
items.note: Upload is always asked for (apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/approvalPolicy.ts).

items.where: More > Extension settings > Permissions
steps: Click More in the side panel, then Extension settings.
Click Permissions and find the Browser access section and the Browser control choice (Auto, Ask first, Full access, YOLO).
Open a normal website, then reopen Options and use Add or Remove for the current site in the approved sites list.
Under Blocked sites click Block for a site, then check that site is removed from approved sites and AGI no longer reads it.
items.needs: a normal website tab to test with
items.note: The site-access card in chat offers Allow for this task, Always allow on this site and Decline (apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json).

items.where: Computer Use tab > Assistant steps > Agent finished
steps: Run a short Computer Use task and wait for it to finish.
Open Assistant steps and look at the last entry titled 'Agent finished'.
Check its text lists what was done and the result.
Open the Chat tab and check it shows 'The browser task finished.' followed by the report.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account and an approved site
items.note: The chat summary text is in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts.

items.where: Computer Use tab > setup card, after opening an ordinary website: the button "Allow browser control on <site>" (also under Extension settings > Permissions > Grant full browser control)
steps: Sign in to AGI in the side panel and open an ordinary website (not a Chrome page or the Web Store).
Click the "Computer Use" tab at the top of the side panel.
Read the card: its headline is "This grants full DevTools-Protocol control" and its title is "Let AGI act on <site>".
Click "Allow browser control on <site>" and accept Chrome's site-access prompt.
Compare with Expected: the card should close and the line "Works on <site>" should appear under the task box.
items.needs: a signed-in account and an ordinary website open
items.note: Setup is one consent card, not a multi-step wizard; the code does not show a separate guided flow.

items.where: Computer Use tab > Assistant steps (screenshot entries appear as the task runs)
steps: Open an ordinary website and sign in to AGI.
Click the "Computer Use" tab, approve the site if asked, type a short task and click "Start".
Click "Assistant steps" to open the step list if it is closed.
Watch the steps appear while AGI works.
Compare with Expected: screenshot steps should show a small picture of the page AGI sees at that moment.
items.needs: a signed-in account and an ordinary website open
items.note: The code shows screenshot steps as images but does not confirm whether the step list starts open or closed.

items.where: On the web page itself during a run: a coloured arrow pointer moves to each click target and a coloured glow frames the page
steps: Start a task on an approved ordinary website from the Computer Use tab.
Watch the page while AGI clicks or types.
Compare with Expected: an arrow pointer should move to the place AGI acts, and the page should show a dock with the buttons "Stop" and "Take over" at the bottom.
items.needs: a signed-in account and an approved ordinary website
items.note: The pointer and glow are injected into the page by the run overlay; they appear only while a run is active.

items.where: Computer Use tab > Assistant steps keep updating while another tab is in front
steps: Start a task on an approved ordinary website from the Computer Use tab.
Switch to a different tab in the same window while the task runs.
Return to the Computer Use tab after a few seconds.
Compare with Expected: Assistant steps should keep growing and the run should not show as cancelled.
items.needs: a signed-in account, an approved ordinary website and a second tab
items.note: The code is marked partial: the run keeps going after a tab switch, but the final live check for background screenshots and input was not confirmed.

items.where: Computer Use tab shows the notice "You started using the page, so AGI stopped acting on it." when the person uses the task page
steps: Start a task on an approved ordinary website from the Computer Use tab.
While AGI is still acting, click or type on the task page yourself.
Compare with Expected: AGI should stop acting on the page and the notice above should appear in the side panel.
items.needs: a signed-in account and an approved ordinary website

labels.text: You started using the page, so AGI stopped acting on it.

items.note: The code hands the page to the person on a real click or key press only when AGI is not in the middle of an action, so the tester should try between steps.

items.where: Computer Use tab > Stop (also the "Stop" button in the dock on the web page)
steps: Start a task on an approved ordinary website from the Computer Use tab.
While the task runs, click "Stop" in the Computer Use tab.
Watch the button change to "Stopping…" and then the run end.
Compare with Expected: the run should stop at once and the log should say "You stopped the run."
items.needs: a signed-in account and an approved ordinary website

items.where: Computer Use tab > "How should AGI act in your browser?" menu set to "Ask first", then a card titled "Approve action: <tool>" with "Allow", "Allow for this task" and "Skip"
steps: Click the "Computer Use" tab and open the menu "How should AGI act in your browser?" and choose "Ask first".
Start a task on an approved ordinary website that reaches a form or button that changes something.
When the card "Approve action:" appears, read the description before choosing.
Compare with Expected: AGI should wait for "Allow" or "Skip" before it acts.
items.needs: a signed-in account, an approved ordinary website and a site with a form
items.note: Some sensitive steps are refused outright rather than offered for review (for example a payment), so the tester may see a refusal message instead of a card.

items.where: Computer Use tab > the "Sign in required" chip, then the "Take over" button; after signing in, click "Continue"
steps: Start a task on an approved site that asks for sign-in (use the test account the team gives you).
When AGI pauses for sign-in, read the reason in the side panel and sign in on the page yourself.
Click "Continue" in the Computer Use tab to hand the page back.
Compare with Expected: AGI should carry on with the task from the signed-in page.
items.needs: a site that requires sign-in and an outside account (Google) if the site uses one
items.note: The Continue button stays hidden until the run pauses for a hand-over.

items.where: Computer Use tab > Assistant steps (each action line starts with "Completed", "Skipped", "Not verified" or "Result")
steps: Start a short task on an approved ordinary website from the Computer Use tab.
Open "Assistant steps" when the run has finished.
Click an action line to expand its detail.
Compare with Expected: each action should have its own line that says what was done and whether it was verified.
items.needs: a signed-in account and an approved ordinary website

items.where: Computer Use tab > the line under the task box: "AGI cannot act on this page. Open an ordinary website."
steps: Sign in and make the active tab a Chrome page such as the Chrome Web Store or chrome://extensions.
Click the "Computer Use" tab.
Read the line under the task box.
Compare with Expected: the line should say AGI cannot act on this page and tell the person to open an ordinary website.
items.needs: a signed-in account

labels.text: AGI cannot act on this page. Open an ordinary website.
Chrome does not let extensions read this page at all.

items.note: The same idea also appears for chat page attachments, with a different sentence in src/side_panel.ts.

items.where: More > Extension settings > Permissions > the × button next to the site (titled "Remove <site>"); then back in the Computer Use tab
steps: Start a task on an approved ordinary website so a run is active.
Click "More" in the side panel, then "Extension settings", and find "Permissions".
Click the × next to the site in the approved sites list.
Return to the side panel and watch the run.
Compare with Expected: the run should stop and the message should say access was withdrawn and to approve the site again in the Computer use tab.
items.needs: a signed-in account and an approved ordinary website
items.note: The run-stop message is "Access to this site was withdrawn, so the run was stopped." in src/features/side-panel/computerUsePanel.ts; the removal path revokes browser control too.

items.where: Side panel > Computer Use tab > Task box > Start
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud from the extension drawer, then open the side panel and click the Computer Use tab.
If the site is not approved yet, click "Allow browser control on" followed by the site name, and accept Chrome's site-access prompt.

In the Task box, type a task that makes the agent visit the open page, click something, read text and take a screenshot, for example: "Open this page, click the first link, read the heading and take a screenshot".
Click Start.
Compare with Expected: the agent navigates, clicks, reads the page and shows screenshots in the run's progress. Open "Assistant steps" to see each action.
items.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account and a site you can approve for browser control.
items.note: The run is driven by the agent, which calls these inspection tools only when the task needs them; the tester should name the inspection in the task.

items.where: Side panel > Computer Use tab > Task box > Start > Assistant steps
steps: Follow the first three steps of S67.16 on a page that logs errors to the browser console (a page with a known script error is best).
In the Task box, type: "Check the browser console for errors and tell me what they say".
Click Start and wait for the run to finish.
Open "Assistant steps" and look for the step "Read page console".
Compare with Expected: the step is present and the reply lists the console errors the page shows.
items.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account, an approved site, and a page that produces console errors.
items.note: The step appears only if the agent chooses to call read_console; asking for it in the task makes this likely but does not guarantee it.

items.where: Side panel > Computer Use tab > Task box > Start > Assistant steps
steps: Follow the first three steps of S67.16 on a page that makes requests which fail, such as a page with a broken image or a missing API call.
In the Task box, type: "Check the page for failed network requests and tell me which ones failed".
Click Start and wait for the run to finish.
Open "Assistant steps" and look for the step "Read page network".
Compare with Expected: the step is present and the reply lists the failed requests with their status codes.
items.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account, an approved site, and a page that makes failing requests.
items.note: The step appears only if the agent chooses to call read_network; the failed-only filter is an argument the agent sets, so the tester cannot choose it directly.

items.where: Chrome toolbar > AGI Extension icon (click it). Shortcut: Command+Shift+K, listed as "Open AGI side panel" at chrome://extensions/shortcuts
steps: Open Chrome on a normal web page, not a Chrome page.
Click the AGI Extension icon in the Chrome toolbar (hover shows the name "AGI Extension").
Or press Command+Shift+K.
Look for the AGI assistant to open beside the page. Compare with Expected: clicking the button or the shortcut opens the assistant.
items.needs: none
items.note: Code opens the side panel on toolbar click (background.ts action.onClicked); if the side panel API is unavailable it opens a separate popup window instead.

items.where: Chrome toolbar > AGI Extension icon, then the side panel that opens beside the page, with the tab labelled "Chat"
steps: Open a normal web page.
Click the AGI Extension icon in the Chrome toolbar.
Look at the panel that opens on the side of the same Chrome window.
Check that the assistant (tabs "Chat" and "Computer Use") is shown beside the page. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: none

items.where: Select some text on a web page > right-click the selection > "Explain this", "Translate this" or "Ask AGI about "%s"" (Chrome shows the selected words in place of %s)
steps: Open a normal web page and select a sentence with the mouse.
Right-click the selected text.
Look for the entries "Ask AGI about" (the selected words in quotes), "Explain this" and "Translate this".
Compare with Expected: the menu offers assistant actions for the selection.
items.needs: none
items.note: The "Ask AGI about" label is a template: Chrome fills in the selected text, so the entry reads differently on each selection.

items.where: Select text on a web page > right-click the selection > "Ask AGI about "%s"" (the selected words fill the template)
steps: Select a short phrase on a web page.
Right-click the selection and choose the "Ask AGI about" entry.
Wait for the side panel to open.
Look for the assistant to use the selected text in its answer. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account for an answer from the assistant (not verified in code)
items.note: The code sets a pending selected-text chat and opens the side panel; the answer itself was not traced in code.

items.where: Right-click an empty area of a web page > "Ask AGI about this page". Or in the side panel: "Add attachment" (+) > "Add the browser page", then type a question
steps: Open a normal web page with some text on it.
Right-click an empty area (not on a link or selected text) and choose "Ask AGI about this page".
Or open the side panel, click the "+" button labelled "Add attachment", then choose "Add the browser page".
Type a question about the page and send it. Look for an answer about that page's content. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account for chat (not verified in code)
items.note: none

items.where: Right-click an empty area of a web page > "Summarize this page". Or type "/" in the side panel message box and choose "/summarize"
steps: Open a normal web page with readable text.
Right-click an empty area and choose "Summarize this page".
Or open the side panel, type / in the message box and pick /summarize.
Look for one summary of the page in the chat. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account for chat (not verified in code)
items.note: none

items.where: Open a YouTube video page (youtube.com/watch) > "Open AGI" button on the page > "Summarize video"
steps: Turn on "Page assistant overlay" in the extension's Extension settings first, then open a YouTube video that has captions.
Click the "Open AGI" round button on the page (its tooltip reads "Ask AGI").
Click "Summarize video" in the panel.
Look for a summary that uses the video's transcript. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a YouTube video page with captions, the page assistant overlay turned on, and the site approved (approval gating not traced)
items.note: The panel says a video without captions has no transcript; the launcher's approval gating was not traced in code.

items.where: Chat tab: "New chat" button (pen icon) to start a second chat; "Recent chats" button (clock icon) to switch between chats
steps: Send a message in the chat.
Click the "New chat" icon at the top of the side panel.
Send a different message in the new chat.
Click "Recent chats" (clock icon) and open the first chat. Look that the first chat's messages come back separately. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account (saved chats are not verified without sign-in)
items.note: The code only shows the Recents button and chat list items; whether they appear without sign-in was not confirmed.

items.where: Chat tab: "+" (Add attachment) > "Add the browser page". The chip shows above the message box with "Snapshot · $HOST$" and a remove button
steps: Open a normal web page.
In the side panel click "+" (Add attachment) and choose "Add the browser page".
Look above the message box for a chip showing "Snapshot · " and the site name.
Click the "×" button on the chip (labelled "Remove" plus the page name) and see the chip disappear. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a normal web page (not a Chrome page)
items.note: none

items.where: Chat tab: "+" (Add attachment) > "Add the browser page" on a site not yet approved. A card titled "AGI needs access to $HOST$" appears in the chat with "Allow for this task" and "Decline"
steps: Make sure the site is not in your approved sites (Extension settings > Permissions > Blocked sites / approved list).
Open that site in a tab and make it the active tab.
In the side panel click "+" and choose "Add the browser page".
Look for the card "AGI needs access to" with the site name and the buttons "Allow for this task" and "Decline". Compare with Expected: access is asked for explicitly before reading.
items.needs: a normal website that is not yet approved
items.note: "Always allow on this site" appears only for full browser-control requests, not for page reading; Chrome's own permission prompt was not traced.

items.where: More ("⋮" button, labelled "More") > "Extension settings" (opens the Permissions page) > "Browser control" dropdown, "Blocked sites" list and the approved-sites list
steps: In the side panel click the "More" button (⋮) at the top right.
Click "Extension settings".
On the Permissions section, change the "Browser control" dropdown (Auto, Ask first, Full access) and read its text.
Scroll to "Blocked sites" and the approved-sites list, remove or add a site, then reload the page to see the change. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The approved-sites list is built in apps/extension/src/options.ts without a visible title string of its own; it was only partly traced.

items.where: While a browser task runs: the page shows a "Browser task controls" dock with "Stop" and "Take over", and a pointer moves over the page; the side panel's "Computer Use" tab shows the run
steps: Approve a site and start a browser task from the "Computer Use" tab (see S74.16).
Watch the page while the task runs.
Look for the "Browser task controls" dock on the page and the pointer moving over it.
Look at the "Computer Use" tab for the active run and the page name. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: an approved site and a signed-in AGI account
items.note: none

items.where: Side panel: "Computer Use" tab > "Task" box > "Start". Mode is chosen in the dropdown with the label "How should AGI act in your browser?" (Auto, Ask first, Full access)
steps: Open an approved site in the active tab.
Click the "Computer Use" tab.
Type a goal in the "Task" box and check the line that says "Works on" with the site name.
Click "Start" and watch the status. Compare with Expected: AGI takes control of the browser for the goal.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account and an approved site (without sign-in the panel shows "Sign in required")
items.note: The task box and Start button stay disabled until the active site is approved.

items.where: "Computer Use" tab during a run: "Stop" and "Take over" buttons; "Continue" appears after Take over
steps: Start a browser task (see S74.16).
Click "Take over" and read the message that AGI is paused. Use the page yourself.
Click "Continue" to hand the page back, or click "Stop" to end the run.
Look for the run to stop and the status to show "Stopping…" then end. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: an approved site and a running browser task
items.note: The page dock also has "Stop" and "Take over" buttons (apps/extension/src/features/content/browserRunOverlay.ts).

items.where: More (⋮) > "Extension settings" > "Account" tab > "Desktop app" section > "Pair with Desktop"
steps: Open the AGI Desktop app on this Mac and leave it open.
In the side panel click "More" (⋮) > "Extension settings".
Choose the "Account" section and find "Desktop app".
Click "Pair with Desktop", type the code shown in the Desktop app into the field and click "Confirm Code". Compare with Expected: the status changes to "Paired".
items.needs: the AGI Desktop app running on this Mac
items.note: none

items.where: Side panel, above the message box: notice "Desktop tools are optional and currently disconnected." with a "Reconnect" button. Pairing state is in Extension settings > Account > "Desktop app"
steps: Make sure the Desktop app is not running (or is not paired).
Open the side panel and look above the message box for the notice "Desktop tools are optional and currently disconnected."
Click "Reconnect" and watch the notice.
Start the Desktop app and click "Reconnect" again; the notice should disappear. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: the AGI Desktop app, and a way to stop it

labels.text: Desktop tools are optional and currently disconnected.

items.note: The side panel shows the notice only while the native host is disconnected; a connected state has no visible label there. The "Paired" state in Account > Desktop app is pairing status, not live connection status.

items.where: Side panel: the microphone button "Voice input" next to the message box. First use shows "Before you dictate" with "Not now" and "Continue"
steps: Open the side panel and click the microphone button labelled "Voice input".
Read the notice and click "Continue".
Allow the microphone when Chrome asks.
Speak a sentence and look for the words to appear in the message box. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a microphone and a Chrome build with speech recognition (on an unsupported browser the button is disabled and shows "Voice input is not supported in this browser")

labels.text: Voice input is not supported in this browser

items.note: none

items.where: Open a Chrome page the extension cannot read (for example chrome://extensions or the Chrome Web Store) > side panel shows "Page access unavailable" with a "Retry" button. "Add attachment" > "Add the browser page" is disabled there
steps: Open a tab with chrome://extensions in the address bar.
Click the AGI Extension toolbar icon to open the side panel.
Read the notice "Page access unavailable" and its explanation.
Click "+" (Add attachment) and hover "Add the browser page" to see "Page context is unavailable on this browser page". Compare with Expected.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Page context is unavailable on this browser page

items.note: The explanation text under the title is a fixed English string in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts, not in the translation file.

items.where: Chat stream reconnect status; "Computer Use" tab run status after the side panel reopens
steps: Start a browser task on an approved site (see S74.16).
Close the side panel and open it again with the AGI Extension toolbar icon.

Look at the "Computer Use" tab: the message "A browser-control run started before this panel was reopened is still active. Use Stop to end it." should show, or "Browser task status is unavailable." if status cannot be read.
Look for "Reconnecting…" in a chat while the connection is lost. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: none (Chrome's own suspension of the background worker cannot be forced from the UI)
items.note: Chrome decides when to suspend the background worker, so the tester cannot force it; the steps only show the recovery messages the code shows when the panel reopens.

items.where: No control. Routing rule that the model menu and chat routing apply; no screen shows text input.
items.needs: none
items.note: Registry and routing rule only; no extension screen or setting exposes it.

items.where: No control. Routing rule for text output; no screen shows it.
items.needs: none
items.note: Registry and routing rule only; no extension screen or setting exposes it.

items.where: Model selector button (shows the current model name) > Available models > All capabilities > Vision
steps: Click the model selector button that shows the current model name.
In the menu labelled Available models, open the drop-down labelled All capabilities and choose Vision.
Check that the list now shows only models with the Vision capability.
Click Add attachment > Upload from device and choose a PNG or JPEG image, then send a message about it.
Compare with Expected: the picker shows image support, and an image turn should not go to a model that cannot read images.
items.needs: a signed-in account; a PNG or JPEG image file
items.note: The Vision filter only narrows the list. I found no code in the extension that refuses or reroutes an image turn to a model without vision.

items.where: Add attachment > Upload from device (then Send) with a model that has an image limit
steps: Choose a model in the model selector (Available models).
Click Add attachment, then Upload from device, and pick two or more image files.
Click Send.
If the chosen model accepts fewer images, look for the notice that says it accepts up to a number of images and to remove some to send. The message should not send until the count is lowered.
Compare with Expected: the request is checked against the model's image count.
items.needs: a signed-in account with file uploads on; two or more image files; a model with a per-message image limit
items.note: The image count comes from model and harness metadata, which I did not read; the exact number shown depends on the chosen model.

items.where: Add attachment > Upload from device (then Send)
steps: Click Add attachment, then Upload from device.
Pick a PDF file and check it is listed in the attachment preview.
Click Send and ask a question that needs the PDF's content.
Compare with Expected: the reply should use the PDF content. The native route versus text extraction is not shown on screen.
items.needs: a signed-in account with file uploads on; a PDF file
items.note: The composer accepts PDFs; whether a PDF goes natively to a model is not visible in the UI.

items.where: Model selector button (shows the current model name) > Available models > All capabilities > Tools
steps: Click the model selector button that shows the current model name.
In the menu labelled Available models, open the drop-down labelled All capabilities and choose Tools.
Check that only models with the Tools capability remain in the list.
Compare with Expected: tool-using chat turns are offered only to tool-capable models.
items.needs: none
items.note: The code gates browser tools on the tools capability (selectedModelSupportsChatTools in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts). I did not find a separate refusal message for tool turns.

items.where: No control. Effect would only show in a chat reply where several tool calls run in one turn.
items.needs: none
items.note: Parallel tool-call support is set in the harness catalog and the server tool loop; no extension setting.

items.where: No control. Effect would only show in a chat reply where the model runs several rounds of tool use.
items.needs: none
items.note: Multi-round tool use is handled by the request path; the cited provider file moved, and I did not verify the current location.

items.where: Model selector button (shows the current model name) > Effort
steps: Click the model selector button and choose a model that has reasoning effort (its menu shows an Effort heading).
Under the Effort heading, look at the rows. Each row name comes from the effort label list (Direct, Brief, Quick, Balanced, Deep, Extended, Maximum); only the levels the model supports appear.
Click a different level and check the row shows as selected and the model badge shows that level.
If a higher level is locked, check its row says Available on [plan] and higher plans.
Compare with Expected: only the model's supported levels are offered and sent.
items.needs: a signed-in account; a model with effort levels; a Free or lower-plan account to see locked levels
items.note: The Effort section shows only for a model with effort levels; Auto shows effort only after routing.

items.where: No control. Transport choice is internal and is not shown on screen.
items.needs: none
items.note: No extension setting or screen exposes streaming support; the cited provider file moved, and I did not verify the current location.

items.where: No control. Prompt-cache routing has no screen in the extension.
items.needs: none
items.note: Cache class and routing decisions are server-side; nothing in the extension UI shows them.

items.where: No control. No region setting or region text was found in the extension.
items.needs: none
items.note: I searched the extension's English messages and side panel for region and route text and found none.

items.where: No control. No retention or data-use setting was found in the extension.
items.needs: none
items.note: I searched the extension's English messages for retention and data-use text and found none.

items.where: Available models list: deprecated models are left out of the picker. No lifecycle label was found.
items.needs: none
items.note: The picker drops models whose status is deprecated (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/managedModelPicker.ts); no stage or retirement label is shown, so the exclusion is only visible as an absence.

items.where: No control. Route differences (capabilities, cache class, retention, price) are not shown in the extension.
items.needs: none
items.note: No route picker or route-detail text was found in the extension; routing ranks routes internally.

items.where: No control of its own. Effect shows in the composer + menu, where Upload from device is listed or hidden.
steps: Sign in and open the + button in the composer. Note whether Upload from device is listed.
Sign out, then sign in with an account that has a different plan or settings, and open + again.
Compare: an option is hidden only when the account cannot use that feature.
items.needs: A Free account and a paid account
items.note: The resolver itself is in apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/capabilityDocument.ts (the quoted lines at :15 and :36 no longer match). The controls read it through applyCapabilityGates in src/side_panel.ts.

items.where: Composer > model button (shows the model name) > Effort and Extended thinking rows; composer + > Upload from device
steps: Sign in and click the model button in the composer.
Pick a model that offers reasoning levels, then open the model button again and look for the Effort heading and the Extended thinking row.
Pick a model without reasoning options, reopen the model button, and check that Effort and Extended thinking change or disappear.
Click + and check whether Upload from device is listed for this account. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: A Free account and a paid account, to compare

items.where: Composer > model button > Effort heading
steps: Pick a model that offers several reasoning levels, then click the model button.
Under the Effort heading, read the list of levels and find the one marked Default.
Choose a different level and send a message.
Switch to a model with fewer levels, reopen the model button, and check the Effort list matches that model. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: A paid account (some levels are gated)
items.note: Whether an unsupported level is left out of the request was not checked in the UI; the cited request-processor line is in apps/web.

items.where: Composer > model button > locked model row (plan name on the right) and Effort rows with a plan name
steps: Sign in with a Free account and click the model button.
Find a model row marked with a plan name on the right side. Hover it and read the tooltip or the row text.
Click the locked row and see that a plans page opens in a new tab.
Compare with Expected. The server-side check cannot be seen from the screen.
items.needs: A Free account
items.note: The plan name shown on a locked row comes from the picker code, not a fixed message. The server check is not visible to a tester.

items.where: More (the three-dot button at the top right of the side panel) > Usage
steps: Sign in and click the More button at the top right of the side panel.
Read the Usage row, including its meter.
Click Usage. A web usage page opens in a new tab.
Compare the meter and the page with Expected.
items.needs: A signed-in account with some usage
A workspace member account and a workspace administrator policy
items.note: Searched apps/extension/src and apps/extension/_locales for admin, organization, workspace, policy and retention text. Found no workspace policy screen. The only denial gate found is connectors coming soon in src/features/cloud-bridge/capabilityDocument.ts. The cited src/side_panel.ts:6168 quote is gone.

items.needs: An account that is not eligible by age or account rules
items.note: Searched apps/extension/src and _locales for age, 18, eligib and adult text. No age or eligibility check was found. The cited sign-in files are in apps/web or apps/extension-vscode, and apps/web/features/auth/AuthSwitchLine.tsx no longer exists.

items.where: Side panel > notice above the composer: Desktop tools are optional and currently disconnected.
steps: Make sure the AGI Desktop app is not running or not paired, then open the side panel.
Read the notice above the composer. It appears only while Desktop is disconnected.
Click Reconnect. Start the Desktop app and click Reconnect again.
Compare: the notice should disappear once Desktop is connected.
items.needs: The AGI Desktop app installed on the Mac, and an account

labels.text: Desktop tools are optional and currently disconnected.

items.where: Composer > model button (Extended thinking row) and composer + (Upload from device)
steps: Click the model button and pick a model that does not offer extended thinking. Look for the Extended thinking row.
Compare with a model that does offer it, where the row is listed.
Click + and check whether Upload from device is listed for this account.
Compare with Expected: a control that cannot apply is hidden, not shown disabled.
items.needs: A Free account and a paid account, to compare
items.note: The Voice input mic button is also hidden when voice is not allowed (src/side_panel.ts), but that label is a literal title, not a message.

items.where: Composer > model button > locked model row (plan name on the right) and Effort row with a plan name
steps: Sign in with a Free account and click the model button.
Find a model row that shows a plan name on the right. It stays listed but cannot be picked.
Hover the row, or open the Effort list of a model, and read the gated level with its plan name and tooltip.
Compare with Expected: the restricted control is visible, disabled, and says which plan unlocks it.
items.needs: A Free account

items.where: Composer > + > Create a video · Upgrade (shown when the plan does not include video)
steps: Sign in with an account whose plan does not include video and click +.
Read the row Create a video · Upgrade.
Click the model button and read a locked model row or an Effort row with a plan name.
Compare with Expected: the surface names the plan that unlocks the feature and how to upgrade.
items.needs: A Free account
items.note: The + row does not name a plan. The plan name appears on the model and Effort rows. What the row opens when clicked was not traced.

items.where: Side panel > an AGI task that needs to read or act on a site you have not approved yet (card titled AGI needs access to the site)
steps: Open a website that is not on your approved sites.
In the side panel, ask AGI to read or act on that page.
When the card AGI needs access to the site appears, read its explanation text.
Look at the buttons Allow for this task, Always allow on this site and Decline. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: A website not yet on your approved sites
items.note: The card is built by buildSiteGrantCard in src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts and called from src/side_panel.ts around line 7902. The exact trigger was traced from code, not run. The approved-sites settings are in src/features/options/site-allowlist.ts.

items.where: Side panel > a failed reply > Switch model button
steps: Send a message with a model whose request fails with a plan, quota or account error.
Read the failed reply and its error text.
Click Switch model. The model menu opens.
Compare with Expected: the user is told to use another model, and ideally which one.
items.needs: An account and a model that returns a plan or quota error
items.note: The Switch model button opens the model menu. Whether the error text names a specific model was not confirmed; a separate notice names the fallback model.

items.where: Right-click selected text on a web page > Send selected text to a local app… (dialog Send selected context?). Second path: side panel history item More > Continue on phone (cloud chats only).
steps: Select a sentence on a normal web page, then right-click it.
Click Send selected text to a local app….
Read the dialog Send selected context? and its list of destinations. Do not click Send redacted context unless you want to send.
Compare with Expected: the surface offers an action that continues the work on another device or app.
items.needs: A web page with text, and optionally a cloud chat for the phone path

labels.text: Send selected text to a local app…

items.note: The destinations are AGI Desktop, VS Code and AGI CLI, built from the constants in src/features/context-handoff/index.ts. Continue on phone is in the More menu of a history item.

items.where: No control of its own. Effect shows in the composer model button > Effort and Extended thinking rows.
steps: Click the model button and pick a model that offers several Effort levels. Note the levels listed.
Pick a different model and reopen the model button.
Compare: the Effort levels and the Extended thinking row change to match the model. Unsupported levels are not offered.
items.needs: A paid account, to see several models
items.note: Whether unsupported parameters are removed from the request before sending was not checked in the UI. The code is in src/features/cloud-bridge/managedModelPicker.ts.

items.where: No control of its own. Effect shows in the composer + menu and the model button after a plan change on the web.
steps: Sign in to the side panel with an account whose plan you can change, keeping the side panel open.
In a separate tab, change the plan on the AGI web app.
Return to the side panel without reloading the extension. Click + and then the model button.
Compare with Expected: gated controls reflect the new plan without reinstalling or restarting.
items.needs: A paid account that can change plan, and a second browser tab
items.note: The refresh code is in src/side_panel.ts around lines 13275 and 16387. Whether the side panel refreshes on its own without a reload was not run.

items.where: Composer model button (reads "Auto" by default) > first row "Auto" in the menu
steps: Sign in to the AGI Chrome side panel.
Look at the button under the message box; it reads "Auto" when Auto is selected.
Click that button and read the first row, "Auto", with its line "Picks the best model for each message".
Send a short chat question, then a coding question.
Look under each answer for a small line with a model name; compare it with Expected: Auto picks a model per request.
items.needs: a signed-in account

labels.text: Picks the best model for each message

items.note: The routing itself runs on the server; the side panel shows only the result.

items.where: Composer model button > "Recommended" list > click a model name, or "All models ($COUNT$)" for the full list
steps: Sign in and open the composer model button.
Under "Recommended", click a model name.
Confirm the composer button now shows that model instead of "Auto".
Send a message and read the model name under the answer.
Compare with Expected: the answer comes from the model you picked.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Models the plan does not include show a lock instead of being selectable.

items.where: Task profiles are set in the model registry; the effect shows as which model answers under Auto
steps: With "Auto" selected, send a plain chat question, then a coding request.
Read the model name under each answer.
Compare with Expected: coding and reasoning requests get the premium profile.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The task-to-profile map is in packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/routing-policies.json (autoProfileByTask). The premium profile has no menu row of its own (auto-premium is not selectable), so it is seen only through the answering model.

items.where: Composer model button (with "Auto" selected) > "Quick" toggle below the "Effort" section
steps: Sign in and select "Auto" in the composer model button.
Open the model button and scroll to the "Quick" toggle, with its line "Answers faster on a cheaper route, good for summaries and quick lookups".
Switch "Quick" on and send a short question.
Read the model name under the answer and compare with the same question with "Quick" off.
Compare with Expected: Quick uses the cheaper route.
items.needs: a signed-in account whose plan includes the cheapest Auto route (the toggle is greyed out otherwise)

labels.text: Answers faster on a cheaper route, good for summaries and quick lookups

items.note: The toggle is only enabled while Auto is selected. The UI wording says "cheaper route", weaker than Expected's "cheapest eligible route".

items.where: Effect shows as a change of answering model between kinds of request
steps: With "Auto" selected, send a greeting, then a request to write code.
Read the model name under each answer.
Compare with Expected: each request is routed by its task.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Classification runs on the server (packages/ai/routing/src/classify.ts). Not visible directly.

items.where: Effect shows as the answering model when a request needs tools; the capability names are in the model menu under "All models ($COUNT$)"
steps: With "Auto" selected, ask for information that needs a live web search.
Read the model name under the answer and check whether it names sources.
Open the model button > "All models ($COUNT$)" and use the "Web search" filter to see which models offer that capability.
Compare with Expected: the request is routed to a search-capable model.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The tool classification code cited (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts) is outside apps/extension, so it was not confirmed in the extension.

items.where: Effect shows when an image is attached; attach menu > "Upload from device"
steps: With "Auto" selected, open the composer attach menu and choose "Upload from device".
Pick an image and ask a question about it.
Read the model name under the answer; open the model button > "All models ($COUNT$)" and filter by "Vision" to see which models accept images.
Compare with Expected: the answer comes from a model that can read images.
items.needs: a file to upload (an image) and a signed-in account
items.note: The attach menu item is in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts; the trigger button's visible text was not confirmed.

items.where: Effect shows in the composer model button's effort badge while Auto is selected
steps: With "Auto" selected, send a simple question and read the effort badge on the composer model button.
Send a hard multi-step problem and read the badge again.
Compare with Expected: the effort level changes with complexity.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The classification is inner logic in packages/ai/routing/src/task-family.ts. The effort badge only shows once a model is resolved.

items.where: Effect shows when the question needs current information; answer carries sources
steps: With "Auto" selected, ask a question about today's news.
Check whether the answer names sources or links.
Open the model button > "All models ($COUNT$)" and use the "Web search" filter to compare capable models.
Compare with Expected: a freshness request goes to search-capable handling.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Freshness detection is in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts, outside apps/extension.

items.where: Composer model button > "All models ($COUNT$)"
steps: Sign in and open the composer model button.
Click "All models ($COUNT$)" and scroll the list.
Look for rows with a lock label and the hint "Opens plans in a new tab".
Pick an unlocked model and send a message to confirm it is used.
Compare with Expected: only models the plan allows can be chosen.
items.needs: a Free account, and a paid account to compare
items.note: Filtering by capability, lifecycle, region and credentials runs in code; the tester sees only the resulting list.

items.where: Provider route is not shown; only the model name appears under each answer
items.needs: none
items.note: The answer footer shows the model, not the provider route, so the health, cost and cache ranking cannot be seen from the UI. Ranking is in packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts.

items.where: Composer model button > pick a model under "Recommended" or "All models ($COUNT$)"
steps: Pick a specific model from the composer model button.
Send several messages, including a hard one, in the same chat.
Read the model name under each answer and check that no "Moved to" line appears.
Compare with Expected: the chosen model is never swapped.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/managedModelPicker.ts reconcileManagedModelSelection drops a chosen model back to "auto" when the plan no longer lists it, which may be a silent switch to Auto.

items.where: Server rule on routing; no visible meter in the side panel

items.where: Chat answer > "Moved to" line under the answer; hover the model name in the answer footer

Send messages until Auto answers with a different model; a line reading "Moved to ..." appears under that answer.
Read the reason after the colon.

Read the small line under the answer: a model name, then a time.
Open the composer model button and compare the name with the model you chose.

items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The footer is built in apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts (answerMetaLabel) and has no fixed visible words of its own.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Upgrade plan (on a Free account; a paid account shows Adjust plan). The sentence sits under the Recommended card on the Upgrade page.
steps: Sign in to the web app on a Free account and open Settings, then Billing.
Click Upgrade plan. The Upgrade page opens.
Read the Recommended card and the line under its price, for example 'N x more usage than Premium'.
Check that the line names a baseline plan (Basic, Premium or Max) to compare against. Compare with Expected, which asks that pricing says what the baseline is and its allowance.
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: No literal '1x' is written anywhere. The baseline is named in a computed sentence ('N x more usage than <plan>'), and it is shown only when a next tier exists. Code plan names are Basic, Premium, Max and Ultra, not 5x/15x. Max and Ultra compare to Premium, and Premium compares to Basic (managed-usage-limits.ts). The exact numbers were not checked.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Upgrade plan, then the line under the Recommended card. Usage windows are at Settings > Usage.
steps: Sign in on a Free account, open Settings, then Billing, then click Upgrade plan.
Under the Recommended card, read the multiplier sentence.
Check whether it names 'per session' and 'weekly' windows. Those are the allowance windows the multiplier scales.
Open Settings > Usage and compare the window names there: Current session and This week. Compare with Expected, which asks that the copy names the allowance being multiplied.
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: The sentence names session and weekly only when the factors differ. When all windows share one factor, it reads 'N x more usage than <plan>' and names no window (managed-usage-limits.ts). The monthly window is not named in the sentence.

items.where: More (menu button) > Upgrade plan. It opens the web pricing page; scroll to Compare plans.
steps: In the Chrome side panel, sign in and click the More button at the top right.
Click Upgrade plan. The pricing page opens in a new tab.
Scroll to the Compare plans heading and read the rows that differ between plans.

Compare the rows with the gated items in the side panel. For example, a gated effort option shows 'Available on <plan> and higher plans'. Compare with Expected, which asks that the differences are listed.
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: The server-side enforcement of each gate is not visible in the UI and was not checked. The comparison table lives in the web pricing page at apps/web/app/pricing/page.tsx.

items.where: Chat composer > model button (shows the model name and an effort badge) > Effort section of the menu.
steps: In the Chrome side panel, sign in and open a chat.
Click the model button in the composer. The model menu opens.
Look for the Effort heading and its options. Options not on the plan show a plan badge and the text 'Available on <plan> and higher plans'.
Pick a model that the plan does not allow, or try to pick an unlocked option. Compare with Expected, which asks that gated options show and the request is clamped to the plan.
items.needs: a Free account (to see gated options) and a paid account (to see unlocked ones)
items.note: Server-side clamping of requests is not visible in the UI and was not checked. Locked manual models use the aria text '$MODEL$, available on $PLAN$. Opens plans in a new tab.'

items.where: Settings > Billing, on an account that is on a trial. The trial notice shows at the top of the plan section.
steps: Sign in to the web app on an account that is currently trialing and open Settings, then Billing.
Read the trial notice: 'Your N-day free trial of <plan>' and 'ends on <date>'.
Check the notice says the trial will not become a paid plan and that the account moves to Free after it ends.
After the end date (or on a test account with an ended trial), open Settings > Billing again and confirm the plan shows Free. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a trial account (the app does not show how a trial is started; not verified)
items.note: The expiry runs server-side through a cron route (apps/web/app/api/cron/expire-code-trials/route.ts). Its visible result is the plan moving to Free. How a trial gets granted is not visible in UI code.

items.where: Settings > Billing on a paid account whose renewal failed. In the side panel, the composer shows the same account state.
steps: Sign in with a paid account whose last renewal failed (a past-due test account), open Settings, then Billing.
Read the notice: 'Your last <plan> payment didn't go through, so the plan is past due.'
Read the next paragraph about no grace period and what stays. Click Update payment method to see the fix path.

In the Chrome side panel, check the composer message 'Update billing to restore Managed Cloud chat.' with a Manage billing button. Compare with Expected, which asks for a defined grace rule and a message on what access remains.
items.needs: a paid account with a failed renewal (past_due), for example a Stripe test account

labels.text: Update billing to restore Managed Cloud chat.

items.note: The code defines no grace period: paid features stop at the first failed renewal (BillingPlanNotices.tsx). The side panel message does not say what access remains; the web notice does. Only the web notice describes the rule.

items.where: Chrome side panel > More (menu button) > account header (plan name). Compare with the web app at Settings > Billing.
steps: Sign in to the Chrome side panel with account X and open More.
Read the plan name under the account name at the top of the menu.
On a paid account, also read the Usage row and its percentage. Free accounts do not show it.

Sign in to the web app with the same account X, open Settings > Billing and Settings > Usage, and compare the plan name and usage with the side panel. Compare with Expected, which asks that both surfaces show the same plan.
items.needs: a paid account, and the same account signed in on the web app
items.note: Per-surface enforcement happens on the server and is not visible. Only the Chrome extension and web app were checked here, not mobile or desktop. The Usage row is shown only for non-Free plans (side_panel.ts).

items.where: Settings > Billing > Upgrade plan on a Free or lower plan account. The Recommended card lists what changes. Blocked items in the side panel name the plan needed.
steps: Sign in to the web app on a Free account, open Settings, then Billing, and click Upgrade plan.
Read the Recommended card. Under 'What changes', check the features the next plan adds over the current one.
In the Chrome side panel, open a model or effort option that is locked. Read 'Available on <plan> and higher plans' or the locked-model text naming the plan.
Compare with Expected: each plan explains what it adds, and a blocked feature names the plan it needs.
items.needs: a Free account (a top plan has no next tier, so no Recommended card)
items.note: The 'What changes' list only appears when the next plan adds features the current plan lacks. Which plan explains which feature is computed from plan features, not checked per plan.

items.where: More > account header at the top of the menu (the plan name sits beside the account name)
steps: Sign in to the AGI Chrome side panel with an account that has a plan.
Click the More button.
Look at the account header at the top of the menu: the plan name should appear beside your name or email, and match the plan on your account page.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The plan name is shown only in the More menu account header. The code does not show it on other surfaces, and the header is hidden when the account is signed out.

items.needs: a paid account

Searched apps/extension/src and apps/extension/_locales for renew, billing period, period end and ends on.

items.where: More > Usage row (shown only on paid plans, not on Free)

Click the More button.
Look at the row labelled Usage: it has a thin bar and a percentage such as 40%.
Compare the percentage with the usage shown on the web usage page after you click Usage.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: The row is hidden on Free and while managed model access has not loaded. It shows one overall percentage, not per-window meters.

items.needs: a paid account

items.where: Composer usage banner (appears above the composer when every plan window is spent and purchased credits are on)

Send a message.

items.where: Composer usage banner or the blocked composer message (shown only for a window that is near or at its limit)

Look at the banner above the composer or the message shown when sending is blocked.
Find the text ending in a reset time such as 'Resets in 3 hr 20 min' or 'Resets in 2 days'.
Compare the countdown with the time until the window resets on the web usage page.

items.note: The countdown is shown only for the window that is binding or blocking, not for every window at once.

items.where: Composer usage banner (appears on a paid plan when a usage window has 25% or less left)
steps: Sign in with a paid account whose usage window is at least 75% used.
Look at the banner above the composer.
Check that it states how much of the limit is used and offers a button such as Add credits or Manage usage.
items.needs: a paid account near a usage limit
items.note: The banner text is built from a template in packages/contracts/types/src/usage-vocabulary.ts, so the exact sentence varies. The Free plan never shows this banner.

items.where: Composer, after you send a message when the usage limit has been reached (Managed Cloud chat gate)
steps: Sign in with an account that has used its whole limit and has no purchased credits to spend.
Click in the composer and try to send a message.
Look at the blocked message: it should name the limit and when it resets, and show a button such as Add credits, Upgrade or Manage usage.
items.needs: an account at its usage limit (a paid account or a Free account)

labels.text: Your Managed Cloud usage limit has been reached.

items.note: The shown message is built from the blocking window (for example 'You've reached the Free limit for now' from packages/contracts/types/src/usage-vocabulary.ts). The fixed sentence above is the fallback text.

items.where: Failed reply in the chat, when the error is quota_exceeded or plan_required: the Switch model button
steps: Sign in with an account whose plan or limit blocks the model currently selected.
Send a message on that model.
When the reply fails, look for the Switch model button under the failed reply.
Click Switch model and check that the model menu offers models this account can use.
items.needs: an account whose plan or limit blocks the selected model
items.note: The code does not filter the model menu to eligible models on this path. It only opens the menu. A notice naming the replacement model appears when a saved model is not allowed (spModelFallback).

items.needs: an account at its usage limit
items.note: No wait or wait-until-reset control was found. The blocked message shows the reset time, the recovery button is Add credits, Upgrade or Manage usage, and the side panel refreshes itself at the reset time. Searched apps/extension/src and _locales for wait and reset wording.

items.where: Side panel > chat composer gate (shown when the paid subscription is past due or otherwise not active) > Manage billing
steps: Sign in to the AGI side panel with an account whose paid subscription is past due (payment failed at renewal).
Open the chat in the side panel and look at the composer area where the Managed Cloud gate appears.
Read the message. It should say "Update billing to restore Managed Cloud chat." (for other non-active statuses it says "Your subscription is <status>. Update billing to restore Managed Cloud chat.").
Click the "Manage billing" button.
Check that a new browser tab opens on the billing settings page (/settings/billing) so the user can fix the payment, and that the message matches Expected.
items.needs: a paid account whose subscription is past due (a Free account cannot reach this)

labels.text: Update billing to restore Managed Cloud chat.

items.note: The extension only handles past_due and other non-active subscription statuses in the chat gate (side_panel.ts around line 13434). I found no wording for a failed checkout payment in apps/extension/src or _locales/en/messages.json (searched for payment failure, checkout error and card declined), so the checkout part of Expected is not covered in the extension. The Code line's freeTrialClient.ts:269 is the managed-access request that raises the refusal; it has no user-visible payment text.

items.where: More (⋮) > Extension settings, then the Options item in the left navigation > Appearance > Theme (System, Light, Dark)
steps: Open the AGI side panel and click the ⋮ button in its header (named More).
Click Extension settings. The options page opens.
In the left navigation click Options, then scroll to the Appearance section.
Open the Theme drop-down and choose Dark. Check that the options page and the side panel turn dark and the status line reads Always dark.
Choose Light, then System. Check the colours follow the choice, then close and reopen the options page and check the choice is still selected.

Open the AGI side panel and send a message so that the typing dots or a spinner appears.
Look at the loading dots and spinners: they should stop or hold still instead of looping, while the reply still appears.

items.where: Side panel > model button in the composer (shows the model name) > choose a model, then New chat (button named New chat in the header)

Pick a model other than Auto from the list.
Click New chat in the side panel header.
Look at the composer model button: it should show the model you picked, not Auto.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account (the model list depends on the plan)
items.note: The code stores the choice in local storage and uses it for new chats (applyModelSelection and clearStoredMessages in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts). The cited line numbers 6055 and 6168 no longer hold this code, so the path was found by search and the model button's visible words were not confirmed.

steps: Open the AGI side panel and click the model button in the composer. Pick a model other than Auto.
In the menu, under the Effort heading, click one level, for example Quick.
Close the menu and click New chat in the side panel header.
Open the model menu again and check that the Effort level you chose is still selected.

items.note: The level names (Direct, Brief, Quick, and others) come from packages/contracts/types/src/design-system/effort.ts. The Default badge marks the model's built-in effort, not the user's choice. Choosing Auto clears the effort.

Choose Ask first, then close the menu.

Open the permission chip again and check that Ask first is still selected.

labels.text: How should AGI act in your browser?

The chat vs AGI Work switch is in the model menu as AGI Work, but New chat always resets it to chat (side_panel.ts), so new conversations never start in AGI Work. Where the chip sits in the composer was not visually confirmed.

In the left navigation click Options and scroll to Keyboard shortcuts.
Look at the list: Open side panel and Send page screenshot to Desktop, with their keys.

In the left navigation click Options and find the row Page assistant overlay.
Read the hint: One prompt and response at a time. Turn the toggle off, read the status Page assistant disabled., then turn it on and read Page assistant enabled. It now shows on your approved sites.
Open a site you have approved for AGI and check whether the compact assistant appears (or disappears when off).

Click Settings, which opens the AGI web app in a new tab.
Look for name, photo and email fields on that web page and compare with Expected. Editing was not found in the extension code, so check the web page directly.

items.where: Set by an administrator through Chrome managed policy (managed storage key agi_admin_site_policy, schema title "AGI site policy"). No in-app control. Effect can be seen when an administrator blocks a site during a Computer use run: the run stops with a withdrawal message.
steps: Have an administrator install the managed policy for the extension, with agi_admin_site_policy set to a blocklist entry for a site (for example https://example.com).
Sign in to the AGI extension, approve that site for Computer use, and start a Computer use task on it.
Look for the message that says access was withdrawn and the run was stopped, and check that the blocked site cannot be acted on.
Remove the managed policy and check that the site works again after a reload.

items.where: More > Help > Export diagnostics
steps: Sign in, then click the "More" button in the side panel header.
Click "Help". The options page opens on its Help section.
Find the row "Export diagnostics" with the hint "Saves a redacted bundle to attach to a support request. The server redacts it before you get the file." Read the hint.

items.needs: a signed-in account

Compare with Expected: the id should be quotable to support. Check that the id is shown.

items.where: Keyboard shortcut in Chrome (default on Mac: Command+Shift+Y), labelled "Send a screenshot of the page to Desktop" at chrome://extensions/shortcuts. Inside the app: Options > Shortcuts, where the row is labelled "Send page screenshot to Desktop".
steps: Install and open the AGI Desktop app and make sure the extension shows it as connected (paired).
Open a normal web page on an approved site in Chrome and make it the active tab.
Press Command+Shift+Y (or the shortcut shown in Options > Shortcuts > "Send page screenshot to Desktop"; use the Configure button to change it in Chrome).

Look for the Chrome notification "Page sent to Desktop" with the text "A screenshot of the current page is waiting in Desktop."; then open the AGI Desktop app and check that the screenshot is in a chat, comparing with Expected: a shortcut captures the screen and attaches it to an AGI chat.
If Desktop is not connected, the notification is the undelivered message instead, and nothing is captured.

labels.text: Send a screenshot of the page to Desktop
